rows.raw: ' As you make your way through the foothills, you become aware of a faint voice — a singing voice — carrying over the windswept peaks. Curious, you make your way towards the distant vocalizations. Over a few minutes, the song solidifies in your ears as a woman's voice giving life to a hauntingly beautiful melody, as entrancing and sorrowful as winter's twilight. Your feet carry you forward of their own accord, drawn forward by the mysterious melody until you're cresting a cliffside, and looking down over a rocky caldera. "Oh, please, [pc.name]," Agnimitra scoffs, batting you on the shoulder. With a jolt, you realize where you are: far off the beaten path as your feet took you towards the songstress. You don’t remember heading off the path at all. "I thought I trained you better than that." Agnimitra laughs as she takes point, confidently striding ahead of you towards the sound of the singing voice. From the sway of her gait, she’s totally unphased by whatever coercive magic is in the singing voice. "I’m pretty sure I know that voice," she says to you, but keeping her eyes forward. "I’m sure she’ll get a real kick out of seeing me like this." You find her sitting atop a pillar of stone; a woman of tremendous, almost mountainous proportions whose dark, avian legs hang lazily from the side of her elevated perch, spread apart to utterly expose a gaping dark womanhood. The thighs and hips around it draw your eye even more urgently than her bare sex, however: her curves are immensely plump, curvaceous in ways only a fertility goddess could dream up. You couldn’t get your arms around her waist if you tried, and if you did, you’d doubtless be going face-first into an overwhelming pair of breasts at the same time, each capped by a broad teat as black as night. The fact that her arms are covered in feathers, sprouting into a broad pair of wings, or that her ears are sweeping, long points of tapered flesh adorned with a dozen jeweled piercings are mere afterthoughts to the shocking, unnervingly arousing sight of her voluptuous, fertile body. Her song fades on a long, throaty note, abating into echoes that cascade off the hills surrounding you. Slowly, she turns her gaze to regard you, showing off a pair of dark-golden eyes and plump, rose-red lips that purse in an expression of curiosity and amusement. "Oh, what have we here?" she drawls, her accent light and lyrical. "[party.solo |A moth |A few moths ] drawn to flame–" "Shaedra!" Agnimitra yells shrilly, making you jump on the spot. She sounds like a mother chastising a child that’s acting up; you hardly expected her, upbeat, zest-for-life Agnimitra to have that sort of energy in her. "I know traditional Tronarii garb doesn’t leave much to the imagination, but you’re acting like a lighthouse for every warm-blooded sailor from here to the other side of the sea of Kacia! Put on some pants!" The womanly harpy regards Agnimitra with some surprise, tilting her head and furrowing her brow. She doesn’t respond immediately; she sits on her pillar, studying Agnimitra with narrowed eyes as if she didn’t understand what she was seeing. "How do you know my name?" she asks. "Have we met?" Agnimitra scoffs, both edges of her mouth curling upward into a smarmy, excited smile. That was just the question she wanted to be asked. "Don’t tell me to don’t recognize Great-Grandma Agni," she says, putting her left hand on her hip. She raises her right, bringing her middle finger to her thumb, and with a snap, her thumb lights on fire. The harpy rears back suddenly, doing a double-take. Her jaw hangs slack as she realizes who she’s speaking with, and she gracefully drops from her pillar, flapping her wings once before hitting the ground. "Agni?" she asks. "I mean... Agnimitra?" "There aren’t a whole lot of undying phoenixes in the world," she answers with a laugh, flicking her wrist once to snuff the flame on her thumb. "And if I’ve told you once, Shaedra, I’ve told you a thousand times: we’re family. If calling me Agni is more comfortable, then call me Agni." The harpy matron, Shaedra, approaches Agnimitra almost cautiously. Her right hand reaches forward and eventually cups her left cheek, the sharp talon of her thumb caressing the plush, healthy skin. "It’s really you," she says under her breath, unable to believe the words coming out of her own mouth. "You look so..." "Healthy?" Agnimitra asks boastfully, placing both hands on her hips and stroking a pose that naturally draws your eye to her bared midriff. "Exuberant? Lively?" "Young." Agnimitra holds the pose for a moment longer, letting the word hang in the air between them. She holds her breath in a deliberate attempt to make the situation seem starcher and more awkward than it already is. Eventually, she lets out a long, stale exhale through her nose, but her smile hasn’t waned. "Sorry if this is a bit much to take in," Agnimitra says earnest as she reaches up to gently grip onto Shaedra’s hand, holding it in hers for a moment. "I know seeing Great-Grandma Agni forty years younger might come as a shock. Like I told everyone, I, uh... tend not to stick around whenever time is up, which is why I disappeared that night a while back. Sometimes, people don’t like seeing their frail ol’ grandma getting reborn." She shakes her head once, motioning towards you. The fiery plumes on her head crackle with energy from the sudden movement. "Circumstances are a little different this time, is all." Shaedra glances toward you, taking in your features from her grounded level. Her eyes go from yours, down to your [pc.feet], and back up. "Shaedra, this is [pc.name]," Agnimitra says, turning her body as she motions to you with her free hand without letting go of the harpy matron’s. Agnimitra’s blue-red eyes lock onto yours, turning to crescents underneath her rising cheeks. "I couldn’t make it to the Temple – time ran out by the time I got to that shoddy fortress between there and Hawkethorne. But [pc.name] was there to bring my remains the rest of the way, and they’ve been stuck to my side like a thorn I can’t pull out." Shaedra smirks – she knows that ‘Great-Grandma Agni’ might be embellishing some facts. "Then that makes you a family friend," she says. "Girls! Change of plans!" You hear rustling all around you, coming from the rocky outcroppings of the caldera you’ve wandered into. Emerging from the cliffsides above you are a trio of much smaller bird-girls, each of them wearing a number of colorful garbs, scarves, and rags – and serving to conceal about as much as the broodmother matron. Although they don’t share Shaedra’s proportions, none of them look... ‘inexperienced’ when it comes to laying eggs. Dangling off each of their hips are small, curved daggers, ready to be pulled out and used at a moment’s notice. However, none of them have their attention on you: as soon as they see Agnimitra’s plumage, they’re quick to rush up to her instead. "Great-Grandma Agni, is that really you?" one of them asks. "Yes, it’s really me!" she answers with a laugh. Another of the girls pokes her taloned fingers into Agnimitra’s wings, causing the plumage to flare up very slightly. "Hey!" she laughs, pulling her arm away, "come on, I just said it’s really me!" "You’ll have to forgive them, Agnim – Agni," Shaedra says, standing upright with her hands folded in front of her belly. "It’s not like any of us have, you know... ever seen you like this before. We’ve only ever known you... as we’ve known you." The third of the girls, though, pays Agnimitra a token amount of interest before turning her attention to you. She, like the other girls, gets rather handsy all of a sudden, reaching for your arm and lifting it away to try and get a better look at you and your form. [pc.isDK |You quickly yank it away and assume a more defensive stance. She gets one, and only because she’s apparently related to Agnimitra. You were lured into a caldera and it’s obvious from the weapons on the girls’ hips that they were looking to jump you. She immediately gets the message that she’s not going to get another. |And you let her, although you have to admit, this feels kind of uncomfortable: you’ve been lured into a caldera, with only one way in or out, and if it weren’t for Agnimitra, you would have been ambushed by a handful of harpies. You’re not sure how you’re meant to feel. ] "So," the third girl asks, turning towards Shaedra and Agnimitra. "Not [party.som | |this one |these ones ], right?" "Yeah, about that," Agnimitra says, suddenly taking on a very different tone: the same ‘angry mom’ tone she had when she first called Shaedra’s name. "Look, I don’t want to spoil the reunion with the new and – actually, I guess this is technically the ‘old’ me," she says, laughing as she rolls her fingers up the smooth skin of her stomach. But, just as quickly, she reverts. "Point is, Shaedra, I get that times are tough and that the world’s a mess. But whatever you were about to do to [pc.name] isn’t the solution." Shaedra visibly shrinks away. With just a few sentences, Agnimitra’s cowed a woman that must be twice Agnimitra’s weight in her breasts and thighs alone. "Um," she answers, pursing her lips and turning her eyes askance. "I’m not mad," Agnimitra says, tilting her head to one side. Those three words are enough for Shaedra to relax her shoulders. "Like I said, times are tough. Just... there are other ways to help provide for the family." Agnimitra’s eyes, for a brief moment, travel down Shaedra’s body. "I’m sure you’ll think of something." The matron’s dark cheeks turn rosy red – frankly, an unusual sight for someone that looks as... full and imposing as her. "Are you heading back home?" she asks. "Now that you’ve been reborn? The others would love to see you in your prime." "Dunno yet," Agnimitra replies with a non-committal shrug. "Maybe! The Windy Peaks aren’t that far away, after all. We’ll just have to see where the wind takes us." She pulls the matron in, hugging her by the shoulders – a proper hug is probably impossible with a chest like hers. "Do me a favor and beat us there, would you? Let them know to expect me? If seeing me like this was a shock to you, I can’t imagine how much of a racket the bathhouse would make if I just dropped in unannounced." "Yes, Agnimi – Agni," Shaedra answers as she spreads her wings and crouches down, getting ready to launch. "And stop getting my great great great great-granddaughters involved with whatever ugly plots you have to steal someone’s money," she continues. [pc.hasCock |"Hopefully that’s all you were after!" ] "Yes, Agni." "And one more thing!" Shaedra pauses, looking over her shoulder towards Agnimitra, still wound up and ready to launch. You recognize the look on her face all too well: the expression of a child being nagged by an overbearing parent, just waiting for them to stop so they can finally get going. "Nah, I’m just messing with you," Agnimitra laughs, waving her off. "Get out of here, all of you. I’ll see you at home." With that, all four of the harpies take wing, the wind rustling around you as they launch off the ground and head towards the not-too-distant mountaintops. Agnimitra remains with you in the caldera, watching them go. [pc.isDK |You casually mention that it’s somewhat hard to believe that that one harpy with the big tits is related to her. Agnimitra laughs raucously. "You don’t have much of a filter, do you, [pc.name]? I like that! I hate walking on eggshells too, and not just for the obvious reasons." She places one hand on her hip as she looks down across her own chest. "Shaedra is a direct descendent of mine, but that doesn’t mean she’s my daughter. I don’t remember every detail of every life I’ve ever had – heck, I barely remember last week. At some point in the tree, I must have had big tits myself." It would certainly explain a lot. |She, uh... has quite the eclectic family. "Shaedra is a direct descendent of mine," Agnimitra answers, "but that doesn’t mean she’s my daughter. Her particular branch of the tree’s far enough removed from me that we don’t look much alike." She brings both of her hands to her chest and pantomimes two, massive spheres in front of her, bringing to mind Shaedra’s... figure. "Obviously." How does she know that they’re related, then? In response, Agnimitra taps at her head, just beneath her plumage. "I’ve memorized every family I’ve ever had. Every partner, every kid – every grandkid. That, and Shaedra has a daughter with red feathers. If you ever meet a harpy with red feathers, odds are, they’re directly related to me." She looks down at her right hand, extending one finger after the other as if she was counting something. "I figured the math out on this once. It was something like... eight times out of ten?" She’s memorized every grandchild? Didn’t she once say she’s old enough to remember the barter system? "I’ve had a lot of time to make sure I got it all down right," she says with a smile, but then she knocks on her own head with her knuckles. "Not much room in there for much else, though." ]'

rows.original: Your trek through the foothills is interrupted by a thunderous screech from high above — an undeniably feminine, yet ferocious warcry. You draw your dagger as a band of harpies wings out from the craggy rocks overhead, eyes glinting with greed as they swoop down towards you. Before they make contact, though, the group breaks off: only one of their number lands. Before the wingleader even opens her mouth, though, Agnimitra steps forward, placing herself between you and her. "Really, Zhara?" she asks, shrugging her shoulders and lifting her hands upward, gesticulating at the whole display flippantly. "The shouting? The screeching? Making yourself as obvious as possible?" The wingleader takes a step back, furrowing her brow at how brazen Agnimitra is being. "I don’t know how you know my name, but you need to back off," she warns, twirling her spear in her hands and getting into an offensive stance, pointing its tip towards Agnimitra, right at her chest. "I’m not afraid to make things messy!" "Uh huh," Agnimitra responds – and places her hand on the spear, gripping it just beneath the metal head and lowering its angle. The wingleader could still easily thrust forward and run the point through her stomach, but the [silly |power move |gesture ] is obvious to everyone. "Even if you ran me through, there’s nothing you can do to the Immortal Phoenix that she hasn’t been through already." Agnimitra pauses, a smug, shit-eating grin on her face as she stares down the wingleader. The woman pauses, her face scrunching further in confusion, but, true to Agnimitra’s confidence, she doesn’t make any attempt to gut your companion. "Still need convincing, Zhara?" Agnimitra asks. She lifts her free hand and brings her middle finger and thumb together – and with a snap, her thumb alights like a candle. Instantly, Zhara’s demeanor changes: she leaps up in surprise and she tosses her spear aside, making sure that the sharpened point falls harmlessly away from them both. "Great Grandma Agni?" she asks, her words coming out a bit strained, as if she can’t believe she’s saying them. Her hands reach up to cup Agnimitra’s cheeks as her eyes trail up and down her body. "Holy shit, look at you! I’ve never seen you so..." "Healthy?" Agnimitra asks boastfully, placing both hands on her hips and stroking a pose that naturally draws your eye to her bared midriff. "Exuberant? Lively?" "Young!" Agnimitra laughs, letting go of her silly pose. "Every generation gets to witness it once," she replies. "I’m lucky I caught you like this while you still have your own youth. Older harpies, uh... tend to not like it when I regenerate." "Girls, stand down!" Zhara commands, motioning to the other harpy brigands surrounding you. Some of them do so immediately; some of them hesitate, still trying to process what, exactly, it is that they’re seeing. But none of them look upon Agnimitra as though this is some big shock: the legend of the phoenix is well known through harpydom, it seems. "This is," Zhara says, stuttering through her words, totally overwhelmed at the sight of Agnimitra and her youth. "I’ve – I mean, I always believed your stories. Nobody can wield fire like you can! It’s just – I never imagined...!" "Take a breath," Agnimitra says, cupping her hands beneath her chest and lifting upwards as she takes a deep breath, then lowering them as she exhales. Zhara, however, does no such thing as she stutters and dances on the spot. She is, after all, staring at a living legend – and perhaps the title ‘Great-Grandma’ has some credence to it. They look modestly similar, after all. But as Zhara’s excitement starts to reach its height, it suddenly deflates, and she narrows her eyes and furrows her brow at Agnimitra. "Great-Grandma, where did you go?" she asks, and she suddenly gives Agnimitra a rough shove in the shoulder. "You just up and vanished one night without telling anyone! We were all worried sick; do you have any idea how hard we all looked to find you?" Agnimitra’s normally upbeat and optimistic attitude evaporates at the chastising. "I just told you: sometimes, people don’t like it when they see their frail old grandma being reborn. My time was up. It’s natural to grieve and mourn the death of someone you love – when that person comes back, not everyone reacts with open arms like you are. No amount of being a living legend with a sprawling history of death-and-rebirth like mine can prepare someone for that kind of shock." "Now, that said!" Agnimitra says, perking back up so suddenly that it causes her plumage to flare with the movement. "Let’s not sour this reunion any further, huh? What’s important is that I’m back!" Zhara’s brow stays furrowed for a moment – but eventually, a smile cracks her lips, and she can’t help but laugh, if only for the sake of laughing. "I guess that’s true. You’re going to have a hell of a story for the others in the Peaks, though." "They already know it," Agnimitra reminds her. "Although – let me introduce you to [pc.name]." She turns, her whole body spinning away from Zhara to face you, offering her hand to you to pull you towards them both. "Zhara, this is [pc.name]. I ‘disappeared’ that night because I was trying to get to the Temple just past that old fortress north of Hawkethorne, but I, uh... didn’t make it. If it weren’t for [pc.name], who knows when I would have been reborn? It could have been years, especially in this cold-ass dump." [zhara.fucked |You two have met before. Although, you admit that it’s nice to have been formally introduced in more amicable terms. However, possibly for Agnimitra’s sake, Zhara is quick to pretend that this is the first time you two have ever seen each other. |You don’t remember if you and this wingleader named Zhara have ever been formally introduced, actually. ] "And you helped her get to the Temple?" Zhara asks. You answer that, technically, no: Agnimitra was literal when she said that she ‘didn’t make it’ to the Temple. You brought her remains there. "Well, that still makes you a family friend." "Yeah, about that," Agnimitra says, snapping her fingers again, although her thumb doesn’t erupt into flame this time. She steps into Zhara’s space and wraps her arm around her shoulders. "Look, Zhara. You’re old enough to understand the consequences of your own actions–" Zhara laughs. "Here it comes," she says as she rolls her eyes. "Good to know that no matter how old or young you are, Great-Grandma Agni, your nagging – I’m sorry, your ‘life lessons’ are something I can always count on." Agnimitra smirks wryly and lets Zhara’s sass hang in the air before continuing on, ignoring it. "Officially, as your Great-Grandma, I can’t approve of you being a highwaywoman. Attacking people and taking their money isn’t something I can condone." Zhara sighs, putting her hands on her hips and tapping her foot as she waits for Agnimitra to finish her lecture. You can tell from their body language that they’ve been in this exact situation dozens of times before. "That said, the world’s in a weird, messy place right now, and I get that you need to do what you need to do to get by. The family back in the Peaks could always use a bit of extra float whenever you can bring it in. If you’re going to hold someone up for their money, quit making so much noise and get it done as fast as possible. The more noise you make and the longer it goes on, the more likely your target is going to get help." You and Zhara both look to Agnimitra with surprise. You had expected a lecture, but here she is, instructing Zhara on how to be a better thief. "Don’t tell your mother I said any of this," she says sternly, extending her finger and tapping Zhara on the nose. "Like I said, I don’t officially condone your attitude." She lifts her head and looks around, finding Zhara’s two companions, still loitering the scene. "But, you know, if I did, then I’d say that [party.som | |jumping in with three to our two is a good idea. Use your numbers to intimidate your target first. Never jump straight to the spears and knives. People getting stuck up for their money is a fact of life, but you’ll be chased down if you ever murder someone. |it’d be three to three, so you’d probably want to reconsider taking on a group as large as ours. Not to mention, we’re all seasoned explorers; we wouldn’t have gotten this far if we couldn’t fight off some ne’er-do-wells. If I hadn’t got between you and [pc.name], we’d have swept you aside. Learn to pick your fights – and maybe get a fourth. ]" She sounds like she’s had a lot of experience being a ne’er-do-well herself. "I’ve lived a whole lot of lives, [pc.name]. Not all of them have been very saintly." Agnimitra pushes herself away from Zhara. "Now, with all that ‘nagging’ out of the way, do me a favor and fly ahead to the Windy Peaks and tell everyone that I’m okay. Tell them that I knew what I was doing, but I knew that people waking up and finding me dead only for me to revive later would be worse." Zhara pouts a bit, looking up and down Agnimitra’s body once more. "I kinda wanted to hang around my immortal, revitalized grandma a bit more. You know... not a lot of people can say that." "I’m sure everyone in the Peaks does, too. Well, any of them that are related to me, anyway." She pats Zhara’s back with a laugh. "Get going. And try not to let me catch you doing any more brigand stuff when you get back." Zhara motions to the other harpies surrounding you to move out; they all crouch down, their wings spread. "Oh, and Zhara?" Agnimitra asks, causing the wingleader to hesitate as the other girls take off, one by one. "Not [party.som | |this one |these ones ], alright?" Zhara looks back to you[party.som | | | and [comp2.name] ][zhara.fucked |; she doesn’t have to try very hard to memorize your face |trying to memorize your face ] in the few seconds that she has before she takes off[silly |. Now that she knows what you look like, you’d better not go through the effort of changing your face, like, say, [pc.hasMuzzle |losing your muzzle |growing a muzzle ]. That’d be awkward ]. With a heavy flap of her wings, powerful enough to kick up the dust around her, she takes off, leaving you and Agnimitra alone on the road. Once you’re alone, you ask Agnimitra just how big her family is. "Living?" she asks. It takes you by surprise just how honest her tone is. "That girl, Zhara, has three sisters[var0 |. Well... one of them has been missing for a while. Poor thing. Her mother’s been a wreck ever since ]. All four of them and their mother have their nests in the Windy Peaks, which isn’t far from here – in fact," she continues, pointing to a mountain range to the northeast, "you can see the mountain from here. They’re all my direct descendants." By two generations, right? Zhara called her ‘Great-Grandma’ a few times. "Try eighteen," she laughs. "We omit a few ‘greats’ for brevity." Eighteen... generations? That’s... that’s a big family. "Is it? If you could trace your entire lineage through history, your family tree would be just as big." She leans against you, placing her forearm on your shoulder; the air around you gets just that much warmer. "Immortality sucks, [pc.name], and I’d rather not have it, but if there’s any one thing it’s good for, it’s having the privilege of never being too far away from your family." Even still! Eighteen generations – and that’s just one branch of her family tree! Hell, forget the tree, that’s a forest. She said once that she memorized every single partner and every single kid she’s ever had, but could she really trace is all down eighteen entire generations? "Sure." She knocks on her head with her knuckles, as if she was knocking on a door. "I may not have the sharpest memory nowadays, but I have plenty of time to memorize some names and faces." She looks around, turning over one shoulder, then the other, looking for anybody that might be listening. Comfortable that you’re alone[party.som | | | (with [comp2.name]) ], she leans in close. "But here’s a little cheat: if a harpy has red feathers, odds are good that they’re related to me. I figured the math out on this once. It’s something like... eight times out of ten? Something like that." That must help with keeping tabs on that family forest of hers. "It doesn’t hurt!" she laughs, smiling widely enough to show off her white teeth.
rows.translation: 当你正在山脚下艰难前行时，突然从高空传来一声震耳欲聋的尖叫——那无疑是一声充满女性特质却又凶猛无比的战吼。你立刻拔出了匕首，只见一群长着鹰爪的怪物从头顶的岩石间飞扑下来，它们那贪婪的目光紧紧盯着你。然而，在他们即将接触之前，这个团队分裂了：只有其中一个人成功着陆。 甚至在那位团队领袖开口之前，阿格尼米特拉就已经走上前，挡在了你和她之间。“真的吗，扎拉？她耸了耸肩，双手向上一挥，漫不经心地指了指整个场面，问道：“那些喊叫声？那些尖叫声？就是想把自己弄得尽可能显眼吗？” 那位翼族首领后退了一步，对阿格尼米特拉如此大胆的行为感到十分不满。我不知道你是怎么知道我的名字的，但你必须离开这里，”她警告道，手中旋转着长矛，摆出了攻击姿态，将矛尖对准了阿格尼米特拉的胸口。“我毫不害怕把事情弄得一团糟！嗯哼，”阿格尼米特拉回答道，然后把手放在长矛上，握在金属矛头的下方，将长矛的角度稍微调低了一些。这位翼族首领仍然可以轻松地将长矛向前刺去，让矛尖刺穿她的腹部，但是[silly |高招 |手势 ]这对每个人来说都是显而易见的。“就算你们把我撕成碎片，也绝对没有什么办法能够伤害到那只不死凤凰——她早已经历过一切了。” 阿格尼米特拉停了下来，脸上露出一种得意而嘲讽的笑容，俯视着那位翼族领袖。那位女性也愣住了，她的表情更加困惑，但正如阿格尼米特拉所相信的那样，她并没有试图伤害你的同伴。 还需要再说服你吗，扎拉？”阿格尼米特拉问道。她抬起空闲的手，将中指和拇指捏在一起——随着一声轻响，她的拇指就像蜡烛一样燃了起来。 瞬间，扎拉的神情发生了变化：她惊讶地跳了起来，将手中的长矛扔到了一旁，确保那锋利的矛头不会对他们造成伤害。伟大的阿格尼奶奶？”她问道，话语里带着一丝紧张，仿佛自己都不敢相信自己正在说这些话。她的双手抬起来，捧住了阿格尼米特拉的脸颊，目光则从他的身上缓缓扫过。“天啊，看看你现在的样子！我从来没见过你这样的…… 健康吗？”阿格尼米特拉得意地问道，双手叉腰摆出这样一个姿势，自然而然地吸引了人们的目光，让她露出的腹部一览无余。“充满活力吗？生机勃勃吗？” “年轻！” 阿格尼米特拉笑了起来，放下了那个傻乎乎的姿势。“每一代人都只能亲眼见证一次这样的景象，”她回答道，“能在你还拥有青春的时候看到你这样的模样，我真是太幸运了。那些年纪更大的女妖们……嗯……通常都不喜欢看到我恢复年轻的样子。 姑娘们，退后！”扎拉命令道，同时示意周围那些女妖强盗们也这样做。其中一些人立刻服从了命令；而另一些人则犹豫不决，仍在试图弄清楚自己究竟看到了什么。不过，没有一个人会将阿格尼米特拉视为什么令人震惊的存在——看来，关于凤凰的传说在女妖族中早已广为流传了。 这真是……”扎拉结结巴巴地说，看到阿格尼米特拉以及她的年轻模样，她完全被震撼了。“我……我是说，我一直相信你讲的故事。没有人能像你这样驾驭火焰！只是……我从未想象过会这样……” “深呼吸吧，”阿格尼米特拉说道，她将双手放在胸前，深吸一口气，然后呼气时又将双手放下。 然而，扎拉并没有这样做，她只是站在原地结结巴巴地说话，然后跳起舞来。毕竟，她正在注视着一位活生生的传奇人物——或许“曾祖母”这个称呼确实有些根据。毕竟，她们看起来确实有几分相似之处。 但是，就在扎拉的兴奋情绪达到顶点的时候，这种兴奋突然消失了。她眯起眼睛，皱起眉头看着阿格尼米特拉，问道：“曾祖母，您去哪里了？”说着，她突然用肩膀猛地推了阿格尼米特拉一下。你竟然在某个晚上毫无预兆地消失了，连任何人都没有告诉！我们所有人都非常担心你，你知道我们为了找到你付出了多大的努力吗？ 阿格尼米特拉原本那种乐观开朗的态度，在听到这番责备后瞬间消失了。“我早就跟你说过：有时候，人们并不愿意看到自己年迈体弱的祖母重新获得新生。我的时间已经用完了。对于自己所爱的人的离世，感到悲伤和哀悼是理所当然的——当那个人再次出现时，并不是每个人都会像你这样热情欢迎。即便我是一个拥有悠久重生经历的传奇人物，这样的经历也无法让人完全准备好面对这样的冲击。 话虽如此！”阿格尼米特拉突然振作起来，她的羽毛随着动作微微展开。“咱们可别再破坏这次重聚的氛围了，好吗？最重要的是，我终于回来了！” 扎拉的眉头皱了一会儿——但最终，她还是露出了微笑，忍不住笑了起来，哪怕只是为了开心而已。“我想你说得对。不过，你回到山峰后，肯定会有很多故事可以讲给其他人听呢。 他们已经知道了，”阿格尼米特拉提醒她，“不过——让我来介绍一下[pc.name]她转过身来，整个身体都远离了扎拉，转向你，伸出手来拉你，想让你和他们一起过来。“扎拉，这是[pc.name]那晚我“失踪”了，因为我想前往鹰棘镇北部那座古老堡垒后面的寺庙，但是，呃……我没能成功到达。要不是[pc.name]，谁知道我什么时候会重生呢？可能要等上很多年，尤其是在这个寒冷的地方。 [zhara.fucked |你们两个啊满足了要求。虽然你承认，以更友好的方式正式相识确实是一件好事。不过，或许是为了阿格尼米特拉的缘故，扎拉很快就装作你们俩是第一次见面一样。 |其实，你也不记得自己和这个名叫扎拉的领导者是否曾经正式相识过。 ]那么是你帮她来到了神庙？”扎拉问道。 你回答说，严格来说，并不是你：阿格尼米特拉当时说她“没能到达”神庙，这是她的原话。其实是你把她的遗骸带到了那里。 “不过，这也足以说明你是我们家的朋友了。 是的，就是关于这个，”阿格尼米特拉说着，又打了个响指，不过这次她的拇指并没有喷出火焰。她走进扎拉的面前，将手臂搭在她的肩上：“听着，扎拉。你已经足够成熟，能够理解自己行为的后果了—— 扎拉笑了起来。“又来了，”她翻着白眼说道，“真好，无论你年纪多大或多小，阿格尼奶奶，你的唠叨——不好意思，应该是你的‘人生哲理’——总是让我有恃无恐。” 阿格尼米特拉苦笑着，任由扎拉的调侃在空气中悬而未决，然后继续说道，仿佛没有听到那些话一样：“作为你的曾祖母，我正式表示，我不能赞成你当一名强盗。攻击别人并抢走他们的钱，这种行为我是绝不会认可的。 扎拉叹了口气，双手叉腰，脚尖轻敲着地面，等待阿格尼米特拉结束她的演讲。从他们的肢体语言可以看出，他们之前已经经历过无数次这样的情形了。 话虽如此，目前这个世界确实处于一种混乱不堪的状态，我也理解你必须要做自己该做的事情来维持生计。如果你能把一些钱带回家，住在山区的家人肯定也会很感激的。如果你因为钱的问题而拖延别人的事情，那就别再吵闹了，尽快把事情解决掉吧。你制造的噪音越大，持续的时间越长，你的目标获得帮助的可能性就越大。 你和扎拉都惊讶地看向阿格尼米特拉。你原本以为她会训斥你们，然而她却在这里指导扎拉如何成为一名更出色的小偷。 “别告诉你妈妈我说了这些，”她严肃地说道，伸手指了指扎拉的鼻子。“就像我之前说的，我并不正式认可你的这种态度。”她抬起头环顾四周，发现扎拉的那两个同伴仍在附近徘徊。“不过，你也知道，如果我做了那么，我想说的是[party.som | |以三对二来应对是个好主意。先利用你的数量优势来吓唬对方。千万不要直接动用长矛和刀具。人们为了自己的钱而争斗，这是现实，但如果你真的杀了人，肯定会被追捕的。 |这样一来，双方的力量就会势均力敌了，所以你或许应该重新考虑是否要接手像我们这样规模的团队。更不用说，我们都是经验丰富的探险者；如果不能击退那些无赖，我们也不可能走到今天这一步。要不是我挡在了你们和那些人之间[pc.name]，否则，我们早就把你打得落花流水了。要学会选择该与谁争斗——或许这样你还能得到第四个名额。 ]她听起来自己也曾有过很多次混日子、无所作为的经历。 “我经历过很多种人生[pc.name]并不是他们所有人都是那么高尚的。” 阿格尼米特拉推开扎拉，说道：“现在，既然那些‘唠叨’已经结束了，就帮个忙吧——飞到风啸峰去，告诉所有人我没事。告诉他们我当时是知道自己在做什么的，但我更担心如果人们醒来后发现我死了，而我却又复活了，那样反而会更糟糕。扎拉撅了撅嘴，又上下打量了阿格尼米特拉一番，说道：“我其实还想多陪陪我那位长生不老、恢复活力的奶奶一段时间呢。你知道的……能这样做的人并不多吧。” “我敢肯定，山峰上的每个人也都想这么做吧。嗯，反正都是和我有关的那些事情吧。”她笑着拍了拍扎拉的背，“快去吧。回来时可别让我发现你又在干什么强盗的勾当。” 扎拉示意周围的其他女妖们也离开；她们全都蹲了下来，翅膀也展开了。哦，那扎拉呢？”阿格尼米特拉问道。这时，其他女孩们一个接一个地飞走了，而那位负责带领队伍的女孩却犹豫了起来。“她没有[party.som | |这个。 |这些 ]好吧？” 扎拉回头看着你。[party.som | | | 以及[comp2.name] ][zhara.fucked |她根本不需要费什么力气就能记住你的脸。 |努力记住你的脸庞 ]在起飞前的那短短几秒钟里[silly |既然她已经知道你的长相了，那你最好就别再费心去改变自己的外貌了，比如说[pc.hasMuzzle |弄丢了自己的武器 |长出嘴部结构 ]那样会很尴尬的。 ]她用力扇动翅膀，那力量大到足以扬起周围的尘土，然后便飞走了，留下你和阿格尼米特拉独自走在路上。 当你独自一人时，你便问阿格尼米特拉，她的家族到底有多少人。 “还在世的？”她反问道。她那坦诚的肌肉度让你感到十分意外。“那个叫扎拉的女孩，有三个姐妹[var0 |嗯……其中有一个已经失踪有一段时间了。真可怜，从那以后她的母亲就一直处于崩溃的状态。 ]他们四个人以及他们的母亲都住在离这里不远的风啸峰那里——事实上，”她继续说道，同时指向东北方向的一片山脉，“从这里就能看到那些山。他们都是我的直系后裔。已经传了两代了，对吧？扎拉有几次称她为‘曾祖母’。” “应该说是十八代吧，”她笑着说，“为了简洁起见，我们省略了几层‘曾’字。” 十八代……那可真是一个庞大的家族啊。 是吗？如果你能追溯自己家族在整个历史中的传承脉络，你的家谱也会同样庞大。”她靠在你身上，前臂搭在你的肩膀上；周围的空气似乎也因此变得温暖了一些。“永生其实挺糟糕的[pc.name]，我其实并不想要这样的经历，但如果说它有什么好处的话，那就是能让人们永远与家人保持亲密的距离。” 即便如此！十八代人啊——而这仅仅只是开始而已一个她家族谱系中的一支啊！见鬼，先别管家族谱系了，总之就是森林她曾经说过，她记住了自己曾经交往过的每一个同伴，以及每一个孩子，但真的能够将他们全部追溯到十八代之前吗？ “当然可以。”她用指关节敲了敲自己的脑袋，就像在敲门一样。“虽然我现在记性可能没那么好了，但我有足够的时间去记住那些名字和面孔。”她环顾四周，一边侧着头，一边寻找可能在偷听的人。确认周围确实没有人后，她继续说道。[party.som | | | 与[comp2.name]一起） ) ]她凑近了一些，说道：“不过有个小窍门：如果一只女妖的羽毛是红色的，那么它很可能是我的亲戚。我曾经算过这个概率，大概有……十有八九吧？就是这么个比例。” 这个窍门肯定有助于她更好地管理她那片家族森林吧。 “反正也没什么坏处！”她笑着说，笑容灿烂，露出了洁白的牙齿。
rows.raw: ' Your trek through the foothills is interrupted by a thunderous screech from high above — an undeniably feminine, yet ferocious warcry. You draw your dagger as a band of harpies wings out from the craggy rocks overhead, eyes glinting with greed as they swoop down towards you. Before they make contact, though, the group breaks off: only one of their number lands. Before the wingleader even opens her mouth, though, Agnimitra steps forward, placing herself between you and her. "Really, Zhara?" she asks, shrugging her shoulders and lifting her hands upward, gesticulating at the whole display flippantly. "The shouting? The screeching? Making yourself as obvious as possible?" The wingleader takes a step back, furrowing her brow at how brazen Agnimitra is being. "I don’t know how you know my name, but you need to back off," she warns, twirling her spear in her hands and getting into an offensive stance, pointing its tip towards Agnimitra, right at her chest. "I’m not afraid to make things messy!" "Uh huh," Agnimitra responds – and places her hand on the spear, gripping it just beneath the metal head and lowering its angle. The wingleader could still easily thrust forward and run the point through her stomach, but the [silly |power move |gesture ] is obvious to everyone. "Even if you ran me through, there’s nothing you can do to the Immortal Phoenix that she hasn’t been through already." Agnimitra pauses, a smug, shit-eating grin on her face as she stares down the wingleader. The woman pauses, her face scrunching further in confusion, but, true to Agnimitra’s confidence, she doesn’t make any attempt to gut your companion. "Still need convincing, Zhara?" Agnimitra asks. She lifts her free hand and brings her middle finger and thumb together – and with a snap, her thumb alights like a candle. Instantly, Zhara’s demeanor changes: she leaps up in surprise and she tosses her spear aside, making sure that the sharpened point falls harmlessly away from them both. "Great Grandma Agni?" she asks, her words coming out a bit strained, as if she can’t believe she’s saying them. Her hands reach up to cup Agnimitra’s cheeks as her eyes trail up and down her body. "Holy shit, look at you! I’ve never seen you so..." "Healthy?" Agnimitra asks boastfully, placing both hands on her hips and stroking a pose that naturally draws your eye to her bared midriff. "Exuberant? Lively?" "Young!" Agnimitra laughs, letting go of her silly pose. "Every generation gets to witness it once," she replies. "I’m lucky I caught you like this while you still have your own youth. Older harpies, uh... tend to not like it when I regenerate." "Girls, stand down!" Zhara commands, motioning to the other harpy brigands surrounding you. Some of them do so immediately; some of them hesitate, still trying to process what, exactly, it is that they’re seeing. But none of them look upon Agnimitra as though this is some big shock: the legend of the phoenix is well known through harpydom, it seems. "This is," Zhara says, stuttering through her words, totally overwhelmed at the sight of Agnimitra and her youth. "I’ve – I mean, I always believed your stories. Nobody can wield fire like you can! It’s just – I never imagined...!" "Take a breath," Agnimitra says, cupping her hands beneath her chest and lifting upwards as she takes a deep breath, then lowering them as she exhales. Zhara, however, does no such thing as she stutters and dances on the spot. She is, after all, staring at a living legend – and perhaps the title ‘Great-Grandma’ has some credence to it. They look modestly similar, after all. But as Zhara’s excitement starts to reach its height, it suddenly deflates, and she narrows her eyes and furrows her brow at Agnimitra. "Great-Grandma, where did you go?" she asks, and she suddenly gives Agnimitra a rough shove in the shoulder. "You just up and vanished one night without telling anyone! We were all worried sick; do you have any idea how hard we all looked to find you?" Agnimitra’s normally upbeat and optimistic attitude evaporates at the chastising. "I just told you: sometimes, people don’t like it when they see their frail old grandma being reborn. My time was up. It’s natural to grieve and mourn the death of someone you love – when that person comes back, not everyone reacts with open arms like you are. No amount of being a living legend with a sprawling history of death-and-rebirth like mine can prepare someone for that kind of shock." "Now, that said!" Agnimitra says, perking back up so suddenly that it causes her plumage to flare with the movement. "Let’s not sour this reunion any further, huh? What’s important is that I’m back!" Zhara’s brow stays furrowed for a moment – but eventually, a smile cracks her lips, and she can’t help but laugh, if only for the sake of laughing. "I guess that’s true. You’re going to have a hell of a story for the others in the Peaks, though." "They already know it," Agnimitra reminds her. "Although – let me introduce you to [pc.name]." She turns, her whole body spinning away from Zhara to face you, offering her hand to you to pull you towards them both. "Zhara, this is [pc.name]. I ‘disappeared’ that night because I was trying to get to the Temple just past that old fortress north of Hawkethorne, but I, uh... didn’t make it. If it weren’t for [pc.name], who knows when I would have been reborn? It could have been years, especially in this cold-ass dump." [zhara.fucked |You two have met before. Although, you admit that it’s nice to have been formally introduced in more amicable terms. However, possibly for Agnimitra’s sake, Zhara is quick to pretend that this is the first time you two have ever seen each other. |You don’t remember if you and this wingleader named Zhara have ever been formally introduced, actually. ] "And you helped her get to the Temple?" Zhara asks. You answer that, technically, no: Agnimitra was literal when she said that she ‘didn’t make it’ to the Temple. You brought her remains there. "Well, that still makes you a family friend." "Yeah, about that," Agnimitra says, snapping her fingers again, although her thumb doesn’t erupt into flame this time. She steps into Zhara’s space and wraps her arm around her shoulders. "Look, Zhara. You’re old enough to understand the consequences of your own actions–" Zhara laughs. "Here it comes," she says as she rolls her eyes. "Good to know that no matter how old or young you are, Great-Grandma Agni, your nagging – I’m sorry, your ‘life lessons’ are something I can always count on." Agnimitra smirks wryly and lets Zhara’s sass hang in the air before continuing on, ignoring it. "Officially, as your Great-Grandma, I can’t approve of you being a highwaywoman. Attacking people and taking their money isn’t something I can condone." Zhara sighs, putting her hands on her hips and tapping her foot as she waits for Agnimitra to finish her lecture. You can tell from their body language that they’ve been in this exact situation dozens of times before. "That said, the world’s in a weird, messy place right now, and I get that you need to do what you need to do to get by. The family back in the Peaks could always use a bit of extra float whenever you can bring it in. If you’re going to hold someone up for their money, quit making so much noise and get it done as fast as possible. The more noise you make and the longer it goes on, the more likely your target is going to get help." You and Zhara both look to Agnimitra with surprise. You had expected a lecture, but here she is, instructing Zhara on how to be a better thief. "Don’t tell your mother I said any of this," she says sternly, extending her finger and tapping Zhara on the nose. "Like I said, I don’t officially condone your attitude." She lifts her head and looks around, finding Zhara’s two companions, still loitering the scene. "But, you know, if I did, then I’d say that [party.som | |jumping in with three to our two is a good idea. Use your numbers to intimidate your target first. Never jump straight to the spears and knives. People getting stuck up for their money is a fact of life, but you’ll be chased down if you ever murder someone. |it’d be three to three, so you’d probably want to reconsider taking on a group as large as ours. Not to mention, we’re all seasoned explorers; we wouldn’t have gotten this far if we couldn’t fight off some ne’er-do-wells. If I hadn’t got between you and [pc.name], we’d have swept you aside. Learn to pick your fights – and maybe get a fourth. ]" She sounds like she’s had a lot of experience being a ne’er-do-well herself. "I’ve lived a whole lot of lives, [pc.name]. Not all of them have been very saintly." Agnimitra pushes herself away from Zhara. "Now, with all that ‘nagging’ out of the way, do me a favor and fly ahead to the Windy Peaks and tell everyone that I’m okay. Tell them that I knew what I was doing, but I knew that people waking up and finding me dead only for me to revive later would be worse." Zhara pouts a bit, looking up and down Agnimitra’s body once more. "I kinda wanted to hang around my immortal, revitalized grandma a bit more. You know... not a lot of people can say that." "I’m sure everyone in the Peaks does, too. Well, any of them that are related to me, anyway." She pats Zhara’s back with a laugh. "Get going. And try not to let me catch you doing any more brigand stuff when you get back." Zhara motions to the other harpies surrounding you to move out; they all crouch down, their wings spread. "Oh, and Zhara?" Agnimitra asks, causing the wingleader to hesitate as the other girls take off, one by one. "Not [party.som | |this one |these ones ], alright?" Zhara looks back to you[party.som | | | and [comp2.name] ][zhara.fucked |; she doesn’t have to try very hard to memorize your face |trying to memorize your face ] in the few seconds that she has before she takes off[silly |. Now that she knows what you look like, you’d better not go through the effort of changing your face, like, say, [pc.hasMuzzle |losing your muzzle |growing a muzzle ]. That’d be awkward ]. With a heavy flap of her wings, powerful enough to kick up the dust around her, she takes off, leaving you and Agnimitra alone on the road. Once you’re alone, you ask Agnimitra just how big her family is. "Living?" she asks. It takes you by surprise just how honest her tone is. "That girl, Zhara, has three sisters[var0 |. Well... one of them has been missing for a while. Poor thing. Her mother’s been a wreck ever since ]. All four of them and their mother have their nests in the Windy Peaks, which isn’t far from here – in fact," she continues, pointing to a mountain range to the northeast, "you can see the mountain from here. They’re all my direct descendants." By two generations, right? Zhara called her ‘Great-Grandma’ a few times. "Try eighteen," she laughs. "We omit a few ‘greats’ for brevity." Eighteen... generations? That’s... that’s a big family. "Is it? If you could trace your entire lineage through history, your family tree would be just as big." She leans against you, placing her forearm on your shoulder; the air around you gets just that much warmer. "Immortality sucks, [pc.name], and I’d rather not have it, but if there’s any one thing it’s good for, it’s having the privilege of never being too far away from your family." Even still! Eighteen generations – and that’s just one branch of her family tree! Hell, forget the tree, that’s a forest. She said once that she memorized every single partner and every single kid she’s ever had, but could she really trace is all down eighteen entire generations? "Sure." She knocks on her head with her knuckles, as if she was knocking on a door. "I may not have the sharpest memory nowadays, but I have plenty of time to memorize some names and faces." She looks around, turning over one shoulder, then the other, looking for anybody that might be listening. Comfortable that you’re alone[party.som | | | (with [comp2.name]) ], she leans in close. "But here’s a little cheat: if a harpy has red feathers, odds are good that they’re related to me. I figured the math out on this once. It’s something like... eight times out of ten? Something like that." That must help with keeping tabs on that family forest of hers. "It doesn’t hurt!" she laughs, smiling widely enough to show off her white teeth. '

rows.original: You happen to come across Agnimitra as you wander the halls of your fort. She has her eyes up to the rafters, running them back and forth, her whole head turning to help broaden her search. When you look up, you see a handful of harpy girls roosting among the wooden beams – you know that you have significantly more harpies than this in your employ, but most of them must be out on their rounds right now. You ask Agnimitra if she’s looking for someone. "Uh, yeah," she answers noncommittally. Her attention is clearly divided. "To whatever you said." Well... if she’s looking for one harpy in particular, then, right now, most of them are out on the job to help [wayfort.harpiesTGN |bring in some extra cash to keep the fort above water |keep undesirables out of the fort’s space ]. But they should be coming back any– Just as the words leave your mouth, a flurry of flapping feathers come rushing into the fort through open windows and doors as harpies come rushing into the building. Harpies of every size, with feathers of every color on the spectrum, rush in single-file, each of them chittering to themselves so loudly and over each other that you can’t pick out a single conversation between them. Just in time. "Alright, ladies, not bad work today!" you hear one of them yell over the others. A particular voice that you have an easier time putting to a face. "[wayfort.harpiesTGN |Report your spoils to the vault and |Check your gear and ] get yourselves back to your roosts; we got another big day keeping shit in shape tomorrow!" The last harpy to enter into the room is Zhara: she dusts her hands together as if she had just finished taking out the trash. A thin sheen of sweat marks her brow, so, at the very least, you can tell that she’s not slacking off. Whether she’s doing what you told her to do is another story. "Oh!" Agnimitra says, her back straightening slightly at the sight of Zhara. When you glance at Agnimitra, you can’t help but notice that she and Zhara’s feather colors are awfully similar. "Hey, Boss!" Zhara says with a wide, genuine smile, waving her hand to you as she approaches. "Who’s this? A new recruit?" Zhara stands in front of Agnimitra, leaning on one foot and resting her chin on the crook of her right thumb as she sizes her up. The whole time, she has a cocky grin on her face, her body language that of someone who knows they’re in charge. "First of all, love the feathers. Your mom gave you great genes." She reaches forward to pinch at the fabric of Agnimitra’s clothing, her fingers coming awfully close to Agnimitra’s left boob. "You dress a little thin for the climate, though. No wonder you found your way here, it’s freezing out there! You dress like you’ve just flown in from Tronarii. But don’t worry," she snickers again, "I’m sure [pc.name] an’ the girls will keep you warm." Despite Zhara showing herself into Agnimitra’s space so flagrantly, she’s oddly calm – in fact, she’s laughing right alongside Zhara, albeit in a much more muted way. "Is this how you act towards every harpy out of the roost, Zhara?" she asks, reaching up to grab Zhara’s hand and pull it back. Zhara’s demeanour suddenly changes, her face scrunching up in confusion. She looks at Agnimitra’s hand, still wrapped around her wrist, and she yanks it away. Her face scrunches in thought as she tries to process who it is she’s looking at. "Great-Grandma Agni?" she asks, her eyes narrowed and her gaze turned to one side, as if looking at Agnimitra through her periphery would help her understand better. That takes you by surprise, and you take a step back – Zhara and Agnimitra are related? They have the same feather color, but... and maybe you can see it in the jawline... In response, Agnimitra lifts her right hand and snaps her fingers – and her thumb instantly alights down to the knuckle in a thin flame, fueled by nothing but her own body. Zhara leaps upright, caught completely off-guard by the suddenness of the flame. She shrinks backward, her shoulders folding in on themselves as if she was trying to withdraw into them. "Sorry, Grandma," she says meekly. "I, uh, didn’t recognize you." "Why, Zhara," she says with an upset tone, although you can clearly tell she’s not. She whips her right hand to snuff the flame on her thumb as she stands upright, bringing her fingers to her chest. "You don’t recognize Agnimitra, the Legendary Phoenix, Beauty of Tronarii, Fiercest of the Harpies, and so on and so forth?" Zhara laughs. "I didn’t recognize Great-Grandma Agni, an old woman one day, and then my age the next." She leans forward, reaching up to gently cup Agnimitra’s chin as she inspects her skin. "Maybe even younger by a bit." "What, didn’t you believe me when I said that I was immortal?" "I believed you! A legend like yours doesn’t come with at least some kind of truth to it. S’just... I never saw it with my own eyes. I didn’t know what to expect." Zhara turns to you, her eyes widening with surprise. "And if she’s here, then you two must know each other? Hot damn, [pc.name], who don’t you know? What haven’t you done?" You’ll let her know when you find [pc.cunningRange 0 70 |someone you don’t know and something you haven’t done |someone you haven’t done and something you don’t know. Both Agnimitra and Zhara snicker at the intentional mix-up – they have the same laugh ]. It’s not like you did anything crazy for Agnimitra: you met her when, well, when she needed help, and you helped her. It wasn’t even out of your way. "Even still, [pc.name], you could have just left me there," Agnimitra interjects. "I’ve seen my share of people. Not everyone is so quick to help an old beggar woman out – especially since I was so old and weak that I couldn’t even fly there from the fort’s bridge. You helped me, and that makes you," she continues, pressing her middle finger [pc.cupRange flat B |right between your ribs |against the point of your chin ], "a family friend." "Yeah, about that. Grandma, where have you been?" Zhara asks, stepping back and putting her hands on her hips. Her brow furrows with frustration. She isn’t angry, but her tone and body language are both genuine. "We all go to sleep one night, and the next morning, you’re gone! Not a trace to be found! Do you have any idea how worried sick Mom was?" The laughter and joviality from Agnimitra’s body evaporates. She frowns, her eyes cast aside and her lips curling downward. The air grows stale with Zhara’s questions hanging between them. "I’m immortal, Zhara," she answers solemnly. "I’ve, uh, died enough times that I’ve learned to recognize when... you know, that my time is, uh, here. I knew it was coming any day. This isn’t the first time I’ve up and left the roost when I thought that I didn’t have much sand in the hourglass left, so to speak." "And you didn’t want us to wake up to your corpse?" Zhara answers for her. "I believe that I told you, and your mother and your sisters, that I don’t leave corpses. But," she continues, nodding her head noncommittally as she tries to weigh her answer. "Yeah, that’s pretty much it. It’s better that you thought I was missing rather than finding one of my plumes inside a bunch of rags one morning." "No, it’s not!" the harpy wingleader barks indignantly. "If you died and left your plume, we would have known exactly where you were! We could have brought you back right away!" Agnimitra doesn’t respond. From the look in her eyes, you can tell that she could, that she had an answer for everything Zhara could yell at her for, but she’s holding back. The air is quiet between the two for a moment – save for the hushed warbling of the harpies hanging about the rafters high above all three of you. "This isn’t a conversation we should be having here, Zhara," Agnimitra says. Her tone is decidedly different: her voice is pitched downward slightly, as if she was trying to mimic her own voice. Zhara flinches slightly at the sound of it – like she’s more familiar with the fake voice than the voice you know. "We’ll talk about this later." "In the meantime!" Agnimitra says as her entire demeanour changes. Like blowing out a candle, she goes from Great-Grandma Agni back to the fun-loving, full-of-life Agnimitra that you know her to be. "I’ve come to understand that [wayfort.harpiesTGN |you and the girls are hard at work bringing in cash for the fort, through completely legitimate and above-board means that I would in no way disapprove of?" Zhara doesn’t say a word. Her cheeks flush red as her pupils dilate. "Uh," she stutters, "y-yeah!" Agnimitra snickers as she wraps her arm around Zhara’s shoulders. "I’m just messing around, kid," she laughs, nudging the harpy back and forth. "Sorra knows I haven’t exactly been a do-gooder across my entire existence. If this place is going to be your roost, then, as long as you’re pitching in – and you don’t tell when I don’t ask – then I’m not in any place to judge. Now, introduce me to some of your coworkers." Zhara can’t help but laugh a little bit at just how flexible Agnimitra is with her attitude. And, to be honest, neither can you. |you’ve been brought into the fort as security detail, to keep other undesirables off the grounds and to help merchants passing through our roads, and whatever, right?" "Uh, yeah!" Zhara answers, looking down and thumbing at her own leather armor. [pc.ra harpy |Although it looks a little loose around the chest and shoulders, you know, as a fellow harpy, that she needs the freedom of movement for her flight. It fits exactly as well as it needs to. |It doesn’t fit her very well, hanging loosely off her chest and shoulders – or, hell, maybe it fits her precisely. You’re not as familiar with harpy physiology as you are with your own. Maybe she needs that flexibility to fly. ] "Honestly, I gotta admit, it feels pretty nice, being on security detail. The girls and I already work well together; it’s just nice being, you know, on this side of the equation." "As opposed to what?" Agnimitra asks, twisting her head a bit, causing her plumage to flare up. "As–" she starts to answer, but then stutters, the words catching in her mouth. "As... opposed to... being freelance. You know, working for ourselves. Taking contracts from whoever to do whatever. You know?" The older bird can’t help but snicker at the verbal gymnastics Zhara has to go through to keep from admitting that she and her gang were thieves. She steps forward and wraps her arm around Zhara’s shoulders, giving her an affectionate hug, but she doesn’t yet let go. "Introduce me to some of your coworkers," she says. "I’m sure more than a handful of them will get a kick out of you being related to the Legendary Phoenix." Zhara’s posture relaxes as Agnimitra guides her through the halls of the fort, towards an adjacent room. Both of them being related by blood, and by only three generations (if the name ‘Great-Grandma’ is any indication), it’s easy to see that they’ll be getting along, at least. You’ll have to ask them more about that when you can. ]
rows.translation: 当你漫步在堡垒的走廊中时，偶然遇到了阿格尼米特拉。她抬头望着房梁，目光在木梁间来回移动，整个头部都在转动，以便更全面地搜寻。当你也抬头看去时，发现有几只女妖正栖息在那些木梁上——你知道，实际上你手底下拥有的女妖数量远远超过了这些，但它们中的大多数应该此刻都在执行各自的任务吧。你问阿格尼米特拉是否在寻找某个人。 “呃，算是吧，”她含糊地回答道。显然，她的注意力并不在这里。“就是你之前提到的那个人吧。” 嗯……如果她是在寻找某个特定的女妖的话，那么现在，大多数女妖都应该都在执行任务，帮忙处理那些事情吧。 [wayfort.harpiesTGN |赚些外快，以保证生计不受影响。 |防止不良分子进入要塞的范围。 ]但他们应该很快就会回来……” 话音刚落，一阵扑棱扑棱的羽毛声便从敞开的门窗中传了进来——那些鹰身女妖们正蜂拥着冲进了这座堡垒。这些大小不一、羽毛颜色各异的鹰身女妖排成一列冲了进来，每一只都在大声地吱吱叫着，它们的叫声彼此交织在一起，让人根本无法分辨出其中任何一段对话。正好及时。 “好了，各位女士，今天的表现不错！”你听到其中一个人在其他人中间喊道。那是一个你能更容易将其与某张面孔联系起来的声音。[wayfort.harpiesTGN |将你获得的战利品报告给金库，然后…… |检查一下你的装备，然后…… ]都回去好好休息吧，明天又是有重要的一天，我们得把一切安排妥当才行！” 最后一个走进房间的是扎拉：她拍拍手，仿佛刚刚把垃圾倒掉了似的。她额头上泛着一层细薄的汗珠，因此至少可以确定她并没有偷懒。至于她是否真的按照你的要求去做了，那就是另一回事了。 “哦！”看到扎拉时，阿格尼米特拉微微挺直了身子。当你看到阿格尼米特拉时，你会不由得注意到，她和扎拉的羽毛颜色竟然如此相似。 “嘿，老板！”扎拉一边笑着一边向你走来，她那真诚的笑容让人感到十分亲切。“这位是……？新来的成员？”扎拉站在阿格尼米特拉面前，单脚站立，将下巴搁在右拇指的指节上，仔细打量着对方。她的脸上始终挂着傲慢的笑容，她的肢体语言完全表现出一个自认为掌握主动权的人该有的姿态。 首先，你的羽毛真是太漂亮了——你妈妈一定遗传给了你很好的基因。”她伸出手，轻轻捏了捏阿格尼米特拉衣服的布料，手指差点就碰到他的左胸了。“不过，以这样的气候来说，你穿得有点太单薄了。难怪你会来到这里，外面可冷极了！你的穿着看起来就像是从特洛纳里伊飞过来的一样。不过别担心，”她又咯咯笑了起来，“我相信[pc.name]而且那些女孩会让你感到温暖的。” 尽管扎拉如此公然地闯入了阿格尼米特拉的私人空间，她却出奇地冷静——事实上，她也在跟着扎拉一起笑，只不过她的笑声要轻柔得多。“你对每一个出现的女妖都是这样对待的吗，扎拉？”她问道，同时伸出手握住了扎拉的手部。 扎拉的神情突然变了，她的脸上浮现出困惑的表情。她看着仍然紧握着自己手腕的阿格尼米特拉的手部，猛地将其甩开。她皱着眉头，努力回想自己面前这个人到底是谁。 阿格尼奶奶？”她问道，眼睛微微眯起，视线偏向一侧，仿佛通过侧眼观察阿格尼米特拉能帮助她更好地理解这一关系。这个消息让你有些意外，你不由得后退了一步——扎拉和阿格尼米特拉竟有亲属关系？它们的羽毛颜色是一样的，但是……也许你可以从它们的下颌线处看出一些区别…… 作为回应，阿格尼米特拉抬起右手打了个响指——她的拇指立刻燃起了细小的火焰，而这火焰完全是由她自己的身体产生的能量所驱动的。 扎拉猛地向后跳开，完全被这突如其来的火焰吓住了。她吓得连连后退，肩膀紧紧地缩在一起，仿佛想要把自己藏起来。“对不起，奶奶，”她怯生生地说，“我……没认出您来。 为什么，扎拉？”她用一种沮丧的语气说道，但实际上你完全可以看出她并不真的难过。她迅速用右手熄灭了拇指上的火焰，然后站直身体，将手指放在胸前。“你难道不认识阿格尼米特拉吗？那位传说中的凤凰，特洛纳里族的美丽化身，还有那些称号…… 扎拉笑了起来：“有那么一天，我认不出伟大的阿格尼奶奶来——她明明是个老妇人，可第二天再看，却觉得她和我年纪差不多。我凑近了一些，轻轻托起阿格尼米特拉的下巴，仔细观察她的皮肤，甚至觉得她看起来还年轻一些。” “怎么，当我告诉你自己是不死之身时，你并不相信我吗？ 我相信你！像你这样的传奇人物，背后肯定有着不为人知的经历一些这话倒也有点道理。只是……我从来没亲眼见过，所以也不知道会是什么样子。”扎拉转向你，眼中充满了惊讶：“如果她真的在这里，那么你们俩肯定认识吧？天啊[pc.name]，谁不要。你知道吗？什么？还没有你弄好了吗？” “找到之后会告诉她的。 [pc.cunningRange 0 70 |一个你不认识的人，以及一件你从未做过的事情 |一些你从未做过的事情，以及一些你不了解的事情。阿格尼米特拉和扎拉都对这个故意制造的混淆报以窃笑——他们的笑声是一样的。 ]其实你并没有为阿格尼米特拉做什么特别过分的事情：只是在她需要帮助的时候，你出现了并帮助了她，而这甚至并没有给你带来任何麻烦。” “即便如此，[pc.name]，你本可以把我丢在那里不管的，”阿格尼米特拉插话道，“我见过了太多这样的人。并不是每个人都会这么热心地帮助一个年老的乞妇——尤其是当我如此年迈虚弱，甚至无法从堡垒的桥上飞过去的时候。你帮助了我，这一点我真的很感激。你她继续说道，同时用中指按了按某个按钮。 [pc.cupRange flat B |正中要害 |抵在下巴上 ]一个家里的朋友。” “对，就是这个。奶奶，您去哪里了？”扎拉后退一步，双手叉腰问道。她的眉头因沮丧而紧锁。她并不是在生气，但她的肌肉度和肢体语言都显得非常认真。“我们一家人都睡着了，第二天早上醒来，您却不见了！一点踪迹都没有！您知道妈妈有多担心吗？ 阿格尼米特拉脸上的笑容与欢乐瞬间消失了。她皱起了眉头，目光别向一旁，嘴唇也向下撇了撇。扎拉那些悬而未决的问题让空气变得沉闷起来。 “我是不朽的，扎拉，”她严肃地回答道，“我已经死过太多次了，因此学会了如何判断……嗯，自己的生命何时会走到尽头。我知道这一天总会来。可以说，这已经不是我第一次在觉得‘沙漏里的沙子所剩无几’的时候，选择离开原来的‘栖息地’了。 所以你不想让我们发现你的尸体？”扎拉替她回答道。 “我记得我告诉过你们，还有你的母亲和姐妹们，我从来不会留下尸体。但是……”她一边说，一边若有所思地点了点头，似乎在仔细斟酌自己的回答。“嗯，大概就是这个意思。让你们以为我失踪了，总比某天早上在一堆破布里发现我的羽毛要好一些。 不，不是这样的！”那头女妖首领愤怒地叫道，“如果你死了，留下了你的羽毛，我们早就知道了。正是如此你当时在哪里啊！我们本可以立刻把你带回来的！” 阿格尼米特拉没有回应。从她的眼神中，你可以看出她可以她似乎对扎拉所能对她提出的所有问题都有答案，但她选择保持沉默。有那么一刻，两人之间的空气变得异常安静——只有那些栖息在屋梁高处的鹰身女妖发出的轻柔鸣叫声打破了这份寂静。 这样的谈话并不适合在这里进行，扎拉，”阿格尼米特拉说道。她的肌肉度明显不同了：她的声音稍微低沉了一些，仿佛在试图模仿另一种自己的声音。听到这种声音，扎拉微微一颤——显然，她对这种假声音更加熟悉，而不是那种她平时熟悉的声音。我们稍后再讨论这个。” “在此之前！”阿格尼米特拉说道，她整个人的气质都发生了变化。就像吹灭了一支蜡烛，她从伟大的阿格尼祖母变回了那个你熟悉的那位热爱生活、充满活力的阿格尼米特拉。我现在终于明白了。 [wayfort.harpiesTGN |你和那些女孩们都在通过完全合法、光明正大的方式为我们的团队赚取收入，对于这样的行为，我当然不会表示任何反对。” 扎拉一言不发。她的脸颊涨得通红，瞳孔也扩大了。呃，”她结结巴巴地说，“是的是的！” 阿格尼米特拉轻笑着，搂住了扎拉的肩膀：“我只是在开玩笑而已，孩子。”她笑着说，一边把那个女妖轻轻推来推去。“索拉知道，在我漫长的生命中，我可从来都不是什么乐于助人的人。如果这个地方要成为你的栖息地，那么只要你愿意付出自己的力量——而且在我没有询问的时候，你也不要主动提及——我就没有资格对此指手画脚。现在，介绍一下你的一些同事吧。 扎拉不禁觉得，阿格尼米特拉在态度上真是太灵活了。说实话，你也不行。 |你们被派来这里担任安保任务，目的是阻止那些不受欢迎的人进入这片区域，同时为经过我们道路的商人们提供帮助，对吧？” “呃，是的！”扎拉低头看着自己的皮制盔甲，回答道。 [pc.ra harpy |虽然她的胸部和肩膀看起来有点宽松，但作为同类的我们都知道，她飞行时需要这样的活动空间。这件衣服的合身程度正好符合她的需求。 |这件衣服穿在她身上并不太合身，松松垮垮地挂在她的胸前和肩上——不过，也说不定它恰恰适合她呢。你对女妖的生理结构了解得并不像对自己身体那样透彻。也许她需要这种灵活性才能飞行。 ]说实话，我得承认，负责安保工作感觉还挺不错的。我和那些女孩们本来就配合得很好，能够从事这份工作，真的让人感觉很愉快。” “和什么相比呢？”阿格尼米特拉问道，她微微歪了歪头，导致她身上的羽毛都飘了起来。 嗯……”她开始回答，但随后却结结巴巴，话语在口中卡住了。“就是……与自由职业不同。你知道的，自己独立工作，接受任何人的委托，去做任何事情。你明白我的意思吧？” 那只年长的鸟忍不住暗笑起来——扎拉为了不承认自己和她的同伴们其实是小偷，竟然不得不费尽这样的周折来表达自己的意思。她走上前，将手臂搭在扎拉的肩上，给了她一个充满关爱的拥抱，但并没有立刻松开。“介绍一下你的同事们给我认识吧，”她说，“我相信他们当中肯定有不少人会因为你与传说中的凤凰有亲属关系而感到有趣呢。当阿格尼米特拉引领扎拉穿过堡垒的走廊，走向一间相邻的房间时，她的姿态变得放松了许多。由于她们之间存在血缘关系，而且仅仅相隔三代而已（如果“曾祖母”这个称呼能够说明什么的话），因此不难想象，她们至少会相处得不错。有机会的话，你得再向他们详细了解一下这件事。 ]
rows.raw: ' You happen to come across Agnimitra as you wander the halls of your fort. She has her eyes up to the rafters, running them back and forth, her whole head turning to help broaden her search. When you look up, you see a handful of harpy girls roosting among the wooden beams – you know that you have significantly more harpies than this in your employ, but most of them must be out on their rounds right now. You ask Agnimitra if she’s looking for someone. "Uh, yeah," she answers noncommittally. Her attention is clearly divided. "To whatever you said." Well... if she’s looking for one harpy in particular, then, right now, most of them are out on the job to help [wayfort.harpiesTGN |bring in some extra cash to keep the fort above water |keep undesirables out of the fort’s space ]. But they should be coming back any– Just as the words leave your mouth, a flurry of flapping feathers come rushing into the fort through open windows and doors as harpies come rushing into the building. Harpies of every size, with feathers of every color on the spectrum, rush in single-file, each of them chittering to themselves so loudly and over each other that you can’t pick out a single conversation between them. Just in time. "Alright, ladies, not bad work today!" you hear one of them yell over the others. A particular voice that you have an easier time putting to a face. "[wayfort.harpiesTGN |Report your spoils to the vault and |Check your gear and ] get yourselves back to your roosts; we got another big day keeping shit in shape tomorrow!" The last harpy to enter into the room is Zhara: she dusts her hands together as if she had just finished taking out the trash. A thin sheen of sweat marks her brow, so, at the very least, you can tell that she’s not slacking off. Whether she’s doing what you told her to do is another story. "Oh!" Agnimitra says, her back straightening slightly at the sight of Zhara. When you glance at Agnimitra, you can’t help but notice that she and Zhara’s feather colors are awfully similar. "Hey, Boss!" Zhara says with a wide, genuine smile, waving her hand to you as she approaches. "Who’s this? A new recruit?" Zhara stands in front of Agnimitra, leaning on one foot and resting her chin on the crook of her right thumb as she sizes her up. The whole time, she has a cocky grin on her face, her body language that of someone who knows they’re in charge. "First of all, love the feathers. Your mom gave you great genes." She reaches forward to pinch at the fabric of Agnimitra’s clothing, her fingers coming awfully close to Agnimitra’s left boob. "You dress a little thin for the climate, though. No wonder you found your way here, it’s freezing out there! You dress like you’ve just flown in from Tronarii. But don’t worry," she snickers again, "I’m sure [pc.name] an’ the girls will keep you warm." Despite Zhara showing herself into Agnimitra’s space so flagrantly, she’s oddly calm – in fact, she’s laughing right alongside Zhara, albeit in a much more muted way. "Is this how you act towards every harpy out of the roost, Zhara?" she asks, reaching up to grab Zhara’s hand and pull it back. Zhara’s demeanour suddenly changes, her face scrunching up in confusion. She looks at Agnimitra’s hand, still wrapped around her wrist, and she yanks it away. Her face scrunches in thought as she tries to process who it is she’s looking at. "Great-Grandma Agni?" she asks, her eyes narrowed and her gaze turned to one side, as if looking at Agnimitra through her periphery would help her understand better. That takes you by surprise, and you take a step back – Zhara and Agnimitra are related? They have the same feather color, but... and maybe you can see it in the jawline... In response, Agnimitra lifts her right hand and snaps her fingers – and her thumb instantly alights down to the knuckle in a thin flame, fueled by nothing but her own body. Zhara leaps upright, caught completely off-guard by the suddenness of the flame. She shrinks backward, her shoulders folding in on themselves as if she was trying to withdraw into them. "Sorry, Grandma," she says meekly. "I, uh, didn’t recognize you." "Why, Zhara," she says with an upset tone, although you can clearly tell she’s not. She whips her right hand to snuff the flame on her thumb as she stands upright, bringing her fingers to her chest. "You don’t recognize Agnimitra, the Legendary Phoenix, Beauty of Tronarii, Fiercest of the Harpies, and so on and so forth?" Zhara laughs. "I didn’t recognize Great-Grandma Agni, an old woman one day, and then my age the next." She leans forward, reaching up to gently cup Agnimitra’s chin as she inspects her skin. "Maybe even younger by a bit." "What, didn’t you believe me when I said that I was immortal?" "I believed you! A legend like yours doesn’t come with at least some kind of truth to it. S’just... I never saw it with my own eyes. I didn’t know what to expect." Zhara turns to you, her eyes widening with surprise. "And if she’s here, then you two must know each other? Hot damn, [pc.name], who don’t you know? What haven’t you done?" You’ll let her know when you find [pc.cunningRange 0 70 |someone you don’t know and something you haven’t done |someone you haven’t done and something you don’t know. Both Agnimitra and Zhara snicker at the intentional mix-up – they have the same laugh ]. It’s not like you did anything crazy for Agnimitra: you met her when, well, when she needed help, and you helped her. It wasn’t even out of your way. "Even still, [pc.name], you could have just left me there," Agnimitra interjects. "I’ve seen my share of people. Not everyone is so quick to help an old beggar woman out – especially since I was so old and weak that I couldn’t even fly there from the fort’s bridge. You helped me, and that makes you," she continues, pressing her middle finger [pc.cupRange flat B |right between your ribs |against the point of your chin ], "a family friend." "Yeah, about that. Grandma, where have you been?" Zhara asks, stepping back and putting her hands on her hips. Her brow furrows with frustration. She isn’t angry, but her tone and body language are both genuine. "We all go to sleep one night, and the next morning, you’re gone! Not a trace to be found! Do you have any idea how worried sick Mom was?" The laughter and joviality from Agnimitra’s body evaporates. She frowns, her eyes cast aside and her lips curling downward. The air grows stale with Zhara’s questions hanging between them. "I’m immortal, Zhara," she answers solemnly. "I’ve, uh, died enough times that I’ve learned to recognize when... you know, that my time is, uh, here. I knew it was coming any day. This isn’t the first time I’ve up and left the roost when I thought that I didn’t have much sand in the hourglass left, so to speak." "And you didn’t want us to wake up to your corpse?" Zhara answers for her. "I believe that I told you, and your mother and your sisters, that I don’t leave corpses. But," she continues, nodding her head noncommittally as she tries to weigh her answer. "Yeah, that’s pretty much it. It’s better that you thought I was missing rather than finding one of my plumes inside a bunch of rags one morning." "No, it’s not!" the harpy wingleader barks indignantly. "If you died and left your plume, we would have known exactly where you were! We could have brought you back right away!" Agnimitra doesn’t respond. From the look in her eyes, you can tell that she could, that she had an answer for everything Zhara could yell at her for, but she’s holding back. The air is quiet between the two for a moment – save for the hushed warbling of the harpies hanging about the rafters high above all three of you. "This isn’t a conversation we should be having here, Zhara," Agnimitra says. Her tone is decidedly different: her voice is pitched downward slightly, as if she was trying to mimic her own voice. Zhara flinches slightly at the sound of it – like she’s more familiar with the fake voice than the voice you know. "We’ll talk about this later." "In the meantime!" Agnimitra says as her entire demeanour changes. Like blowing out a candle, she goes from Great-Grandma Agni back to the fun-loving, full-of-life Agnimitra that you know her to be. "I’ve come to understand that [wayfort.harpiesTGN |you and the girls are hard at work bringing in cash for the fort, through completely legitimate and above-board means that I would in no way disapprove of?" Zhara doesn’t say a word. Her cheeks flush red as her pupils dilate. "Uh," she stutters, "y-yeah!" Agnimitra snickers as she wraps her arm around Zhara’s shoulders. "I’m just messing around, kid," she laughs, nudging the harpy back and forth. "Sorra knows I haven’t exactly been a do-gooder across my entire existence. If this place is going to be your roost, then, as long as you’re pitching in – and you don’t tell when I don’t ask – then I’m not in any place to judge. Now, introduce me to some of your coworkers." Zhara can’t help but laugh a little bit at just how flexible Agnimitra is with her attitude. And, to be honest, neither can you. |you’ve been brought into the fort as security detail, to keep other undesirables off the grounds and to help merchants passing through our roads, and whatever, right?" "Uh, yeah!" Zhara answers, looking down and thumbing at her own leather armor. [pc.ra harpy |Although it looks a little loose around the chest and shoulders, you know, as a fellow harpy, that she needs the freedom of movement for her flight. It fits exactly as well as it needs to. |It doesn’t fit her very well, hanging loosely off her chest and shoulders – or, hell, maybe it fits her precisely. You’re not as familiar with harpy physiology as you are with your own. Maybe she needs that flexibility to fly. ] "Honestly, I gotta admit, it feels pretty nice, being on security detail. The girls and I already work well together; it’s just nice being, you know, on this side of the equation." "As opposed to what?" Agnimitra asks, twisting her head a bit, causing her plumage to flare up. "As–" she starts to answer, but then stutters, the words catching in her mouth. "As... opposed to... being freelance. You know, working for ourselves. Taking contracts from whoever to do whatever. You know?" The older bird can’t help but snicker at the verbal gymnastics Zhara has to go through to keep from admitting that she and her gang were thieves. She steps forward and wraps her arm around Zhara’s shoulders, giving her an affectionate hug, but she doesn’t yet let go. "Introduce me to some of your coworkers," she says. "I’m sure more than a handful of them will get a kick out of you being related to the Legendary Phoenix." Zhara’s posture relaxes as Agnimitra guides her through the halls of the fort, towards an adjacent room. Both of them being related by blood, and by only three generations (if the name ‘Great-Grandma’ is any indication), it’s easy to see that they’ll be getting along, at least. You’ll have to ask them more about that when you can. ]'

rows.original: You explore the layout of your abode, [wayfort.stateABC|noting the many, many places it still needs fixing – but it’s yours. You can’t help but|spotting some places that could still use a bit of improvement, but it, like you, has come a long way. You can’t help but|admiring what a bit of effort (and money) can do to really turn even a strategic fort like this one into a home. You can’t help but] bask in the fact that you went from destitute and homeless to the baron[pc.mf||ess] of a fort in what feels like such a short amount of time. You spot a flash of red out of the corner of your eye, and when you turn your head towards it, you see Agnimitra, the phoenix, approaching you. "Hey, [pc.name], just the [pc.mf|guy|gal] I was looking for," she says. You ask her how you can help her. "I was just in the mood to do some cooking, actually. [hours 0 7 12 5 |I had a hankering for a late-night snack. Well, except, the snack is a full meal. |You need to start your days right with a hearty breakfast, after all! |Lunch has always been my favorite meal of the day, personally. |What better way to put the skills that Sorra gave me to use by making some dinner? ] I was thinking of cooking some [silly |poultry." Poultry? "It’s not weird." It’s kind of weird. "It’s not weird. It’s weird in the same way that [pc.ra human|you|humans] eating, like, a lemur or something would be weird." That’s pretty weird. "Ugh, fine. Steaks, then. |steaks. Something real big and filling. ] You want some? I was gonna make some for one, but I’ll toss in a bit for you too, if you want. It’ll be on me." That’s a weird way to phrase it, considering it’s your fort, your kitchen, your food that she’s cooking[var0|, and you’ve recently eaten already... but| – but] you’re not going to say no when Agnimitra is offering to make you something. You answer that, sure, you could go for some food. "Perfect," she answers with a wide, toothy grin – an oddly mischievous expression, like she’s a bit too excited for you to have said yes. "Meet me in the kitchen in an hour. It ought to be ready by then." Sure. You’re looking forward to it.

rows.original: When you enter the kitchen, you find, unsurprisingly, Agnimitra, standing at the door to the pantry with her hand crooked against her chin in thought. Near her feet is the meat locker, filled with fresh-cut slabs of everything from mutton to venison, kept in a pile of salt to keep them from spoiling. "Oh, [pc.name]," Agnimitra says, turning her head when she hears your footsteps. "You hungry?" ... Is she looking for an excuse to do her favorite ‘party trick’ again? "What?" she asks, reeling backward in shock. "Noooo, noo, what? I mean, pfft, nooo." Her lips purse and her cheeks rise and redden as she tries to keep from laughing. "But, I mean, if you want me to do it, I mean, that’s kinda weird on your part, but I guess I’ll do it if you want. Just because I like you so much." What, was she just standing here the whole time, hoping someone would come in and ask her to grill some meat on her abs? "No," she answers earnestly. "I was hungry, so I came here, and I was trying to decide what I was in the mood for. You coming in after me was an opportunity." She pauses and smirks – an unusually nervous smirk, like she knows what she’s about to do or say might not go over well. "Like I told you, it’s as sanitary as cooking with a pan – but not everybody appreciates the idea of eating meat I’ve cooked straight off my skin. We’re both lucky that you’re cool about it." The silence hangs in the air for a moment. "So, you want me to grill meat on my abs, or not?"
rows.translation: 当你走进厨房时，不出所料，你看到了阿格尼米特拉——她站在食品储藏室的门口，手托着下巴，若有所思地站着。在她脚边是那个肉类储藏柜，里面摆满了从羊肉到鹿肉等各种新鲜切割好的肉类，这些肉类都被撒上了一层盐，以防止它们变质。 “哦，[pc.name]，”阿格尼米特拉说道，听到你的脚步声后转过头来，‘你饿了吗？’” ……她是在找借口，想再表演她最喜欢的那个“把戏”吗？ “什么？”她震惊地后退了几步，问道，“不……不，什么？我是说，哎呀，不。”她努力忍住笑意，嘴唇紧闭，脸颊涨得通红，“但是，我的意思是，如果你想要让我来做这件事吧，我觉得那样有点奇怪你的只是想帮忙而已，但如果你希望的话，我当然会去做。因为我真的很喜欢你。” 什么？她刚才一直站在这里，就等着有人进来请她用腹肌来烤肉吗？ “不，”她认真地回答道。我饿了，所以就来到了这里，正在考虑想吃些什么。你跟着我进来，正好给了我一个机会。”她停顿了一下，然后露出一个笑容——一个显得有些紧张的笑容，仿佛她知道自己接下来要说的或要做的事情可能会不太顺利。就像我之前说的，这种方法跟用平底锅做饭一样卫生——但并不是所有人都能接受直接从肉皮上切下来的肉。我们俩都很幸运，因为你对此并不反感。” 空气中陷入了一阵沉默。所以，你是想让我用腹肌来‘烤肉’，还是不想这样呢？

rows.original: Rumie doesn’t seem to like it whenever Agnimitra does her ‘party trick’. It’s something of a health hazard, for a few reasons. But, honestly, the first time you had it, you remember saying that she was right that meat cooked on her skin doesn’t have that smoky taste and granular texture that meat cooked over a fire pit has. Whether or not it tastes better is subjective... but you’ll just have to have it again to know for sure. "Maybe I should look into coming up with some kind of secret ingredient," she laughs. "Maybe if I cook it by pinching it between my thighs! I’ll take all of that as a ‘yes’, then?" ... Fuck it, sure, you could go for a meal. You’ll just have to deal with Rumie later. "Hell yeah," she laughs, nudging you with her elbow before bending over to open the meat box. "All fun and games aside, it still needs to actually cook. Come back in an hour; it ought to be ready by then."
