rows.raw: ' [var1 |If nobody’s going to answer the question, you might as well: you ask her about being ‘Fiercest of the Harpies’. ‘Agnimitra, Fiercest of the Harpies’ was one of the titles she used when she introduced herself to you. |The next topic you’d like to hear about is how she came to be known as ‘Fiercest of the Harpies’. That was one of the titles she used to introduce herself to you back when you first revived her. Agnimitra is typically a fun-loving, high-on-life kind of woman, but given her status – and abilities – of a phoenix, you could believe that she could really do some damage if she was mad enough for it. ] Agnimitra hums as she strums her fingers on the gittern, making a rhythmless tune to fill the air as she considers it. Her body language takes a visible shift and her expression hardens into something much more serious. The memory of how she got her title is still fresh, despite however many years it’s been. "We know better than anyone that harpies can be real hard[var0 |-" she says, then pauses, looking down at Mitra. "Hardheads |asses ]. Do you have any idea what I would have had to do to be given a title like ‘fiercest of them all’?" A momentary silence. "I always thought that your generations of experience made you a good tactician, or something," one of them answers. She frowns. "Let’s just say that there’s an easy way to make me mad[var0 |." She, again, looks down at Mitra, who looks up at her great-great-grandma with unbroken focus. "I’ll have to omit some of the facts for some of the more impressionable among us, though ]." She strums her gittern a few times, but she doesn’t try to harmonize her voice with the notes she’s making. The music is just to fill the air as she readies herself for the story. "This one doesn’t come with a song, I’m afraid," she says. "I’m known for a lot of things. Queen Agnimitra, First of Her Kind, Beauty of Tronarii. I didn’t want my ‘Fiercest of the Harpies’ story to be made into a song. It’s not really a ‘sing by the campfire’ kind of story." Is it something she’d rather forget? If so, why not just... forget it? "When you live as long as I have, [pc.name], you find out eventually that, no matter where you are, no matter how old you get, no matter how much time has passed..." she stops her strumming and looks up at you, her eyes a mixture between fierce like a raging bull, and... dead. Blank. "The past will catch up to you. So there’s no point in trying to hide it, or trying to hide from it. It’s a title I wear as openly as any other. Just. You know," she shrugs, as a flicker of the old Agnimitra that you know resurfaces, "not in song." Her fingers move individually along the strings, almost as though the gittern was telling its own story. "This would have been well before any of you were even ideas," she starts as she lowers her head to watch her own fingers dance. "Long ago, there was a harpy woman named Luqezta. Luqezta had beautiful feathers: every color of the rainbow, from her long, flowing hair to the short-feathers on her legs. And just for that extra splash of fashion, the tips of her wings were black. It’s hard to imagine nowadays, right?" Her ankle twists idly as she recounts the memory of this Luqezta woman. "Most harpies are one, maybe two colors. I’ve been around a long time and even I’ve only ever seen anything like it a few times." "Was Luqezta one of your daughters?" one of the harpy ladies in her audience asks. "No," she answers. "Luqezta and I met when my wandering took me Izkanti jungles down south. Plumage like hers was..." Agnimitra stops suddenly. Her eyes become glassy and her expression falters, staring at nothing [var0 |just above Mitra’s head |off in the distance ]. "It wasn’t common in the desert, let’s just say that," she finishes cryptically. She doesn’t let the pause or her sullen words hang in the air for long. "Luqezta and I were fast friends. I stayed in the jungles with her for a few months before I convinced her to come back to Tronarii with me. And shortly after that[var0 |, well," she says, smirking down at Mitra before her, "let’s just say that we were really good friends." Mitra rests her hands on her chin and her eyes positively light up. "Awww," she coos. |, we became lovers. I was attracted not just to her gorgeous feathers, but to the way she talked, and the way she could play the lyre. To this day, generations later, I never could play it the way she could." ] Agnimitra goes quiet again for a little bit as she strums the strings on her gittern, letting it tell the story for a few sentences. Her melodies are melancholic and slow, but focused: you can’t be certain, but you think she’s playing an actual song that she knows. One that she’s practiced a lot. "Luqezta and I had a daughter," she eventually continues. "Her name was Torkelie. She inherited most of Luqezta’s colors... although once her feathers started coming in, I have to admit, I was happy to see a bright red splash of red across her chest. There’s no way she didn’t get that from me." You idly wonder what any of this has to do with Agnimitra being called the ‘Fiercest of the Harpies.’ [pc.isDK |Bards always did have a poor way with brevity: either they use twenty words when five will do, or they use five words but two of them are from some different language and you feel like an idiot when you don’t know what they mean. You’re half tempted to tell her to get to the point. |You suppose this is her habit as a bard shining through: ask them to tell a story, and you’ll be there all night. And Agnimitra in particular has a lot of stories to tell. ] "Anyway," she continues, pausing her strumming to adjust the tuning on the gittern’s neck. "Rainbow-colored feathers aren’t really heard of in Tronarii. You have reds, like mine, and mostly bolder colors like browns and blacks. Green and blue is more common here in the Frost Marches. But there weren’t any harpies that had them all. That was only an Izkanti thing. It made Luqezta and Torkelie especially popular among the other harpies in the region." She strums the gittern, letting her finger rest on the bottommost string, warping the sound it makes as it vibrates against her thumb. "I’m to blame for their... popularity, too," she continues, keeping her eyes down. "I wrote songs about their beauty and the rarity of their plumage. I couldn’t not. Feathers like theirs was like seeing a person with three heads in the desert." In a deeply unusual move, Agnimitra stops playing her gittern. Her fingers rest against the instrument’s belly, near the sound hole. She turns her head away, her lips pursed – her expression as cold and stony as she can[pc.isDK |, although you can see, plain as day, the hurt in her cheeks. She’s good at masking it, but you can tell, because you know what that look is like ]. [var0 |Agnimitra keeps her face away from her audience, but her eyes turn to Mitra, sitting on her knees in front of her, looking up to her ‘great-grandma’ with a mixture of expectation and trepidation. She can tell that Agnimitra is upset about something, but her childlike curiosity won’t let her tell Agnimitra to stop. |The silence hangs heavy in the air between Agnimitra and her audience for much longer than usual. She takes a long, deep sigh through her nose, then grips the gittern by the neck, her knuckles bulging. She looks like she’s about to try and snap it with her grip, or to whip it upside down and bash it against the floor, but she does neither. ] [var0 |Forlornly, Agnimitra resumes strumming, although she’s not into it and the notes are bland and directionless, as if this was her second day playing it. "Luqezta and Torkelie... went missing, one day," she continues. "Woke up one morning, and neither of them were there in the nest with me. There was, a, uhh," she stutters, "a... note. A note that said that they had been... kidnapped. By some wandering brigands." Mitra gasps, both of her hands flying to her mouth to hide her face. "Oh no!" she cries. "Yeah, fortunately, they were known bandits in the region," Agnimitra continues. "I knew how to track them down. They kidnapped Luqezta and Torkelie and they were going to pluck the feathers right off their wings and sell to the highest bidder in the Tronarii sands." "That’s awful!" Mitra gasps. Agnimitra pauses, then strums her gittern once. "Yeah," she replies. "Awful." She pauses for a moment, looking down at her fingers as she strums the gittern. The faintest of smiles plays on her lips as she considers how best to proceed with the story. If you had to guess, she’s thinking of how to censor it for a certain impressionable audience. "Well, you know what your great-grandma Agni did?" she continues, leaning forward, bringing herself close enough to Mitra that, if Mitra leaned forward, their noses would touch. "I found one of those buggin’ bandits and I beat him up!" "You beat him up?!" Mitra asks in astonishment. "Yeah, I did!" she answers, stopping her strumming so she can flex her arm. There is very little muscle on it. "I tracked him down and I told him to tell me where he took Luqezta and Torkelie. But he wouldn’t tell me! I said ‘where are you keeping my wife and daughter?’ and the guy replied ‘I ain’t sayin’ nothing to some bird’! So I taught him some manners, is what I did!" Every word that Agnimitra says is hidden behind a pained smile and pushed through a clog in her throat. There’s quite a bit that she’s not telling for Mitra’s sake. It goes to show her skills as a storyteller, that she can tell even the most painful of personal stories while still making it entertaining, at least for certain audiences, all while censoring it but not being dishonest about it. "Yeah!" Mitra cheers, balling her hands into fists and punching the air in front of herself. "Did he tell you where they where?" "Of course he did!" Agnimitra says with a few high-paced strums of her fingers on the strings. "Because if he didn’t, I would have went right back to where I left him and I would have buried his head in the sand until he told me what I wanted to hear!" Mitra laughs at the idea. So do some of the other adults. "So I found the bandit hideout, and I went in there alone. There must have been a hundred – no, two – no, three hundred men in there! All of them, doing dastardly stuff, like... sharpening their daggers, and drinking booze, and... not washing their teeth! Only bad guys don’t wash their teeth, you know." Mitra’s joviality plummets. She looks over her shoulder towards the group of adult harpies standing behind her. "Is that true?" she asks one of them. "You don’t believe your great-grandma Agni?" one of the harpies asks in turn. "It’s true. Bad guys don’t wash their teeth. You can tell if a person is good or bad by how well they take care of their teeth." "So you’d better brush them after every meal," Agnimitra finishes, pushing the head of her gittern against Mitra’s shoulder, without skipping a beat on her melodic-but-rhythmless playing. "Anyway, moving on! They had this cave out in the desert, well off the beaten path. So I go in there, and there’s Luqezta and Torkelie – they’re both trapped in cages! Luqezta calls down to me: ‘help us, Agni! Help us!’ And I go up to the closest table, and I throw off all of the gross, undercooked food on it, and I jump onto it, and I point to Luqezta’s cage, and I shout ‘unhand my wife and daughter, you villains!’" The longer Agnimitra talks, the faster her fingers play on her gittern. Mitra sits up on her knees, hanging onto every word her great-grandma tells her. "But, of course, I knew they weren’t going to just give them back to me. I pull the sword from the scabbard of one of the bandits, right out from under his nose, and I do battle with each of them – all three hundred bandits come after me, but your great-grandma Agni, she’s been in more fights than all of them put together. A swipe here!" she says, swinging her gittern. "A thrust there!" she continues, lunging her instrument forward. "I used the blade to disarm each and every lawbreaker as they approached, and with a swipe of my hand against their neck, I would knock them unconscious. Death was too good for them!" "And the leader, the last to approach me: he was this tall, imposing man. He tells me that his father was a minotaur, and his mother was a demon. And he looked the part! Tall as a house; wide as a barn; his muscles had muscles had muscles. I felled him by lunging between his legs, and as he bent over to try and grab at me, I swung my blade at the belt of his pants – and down they fell, revealing his white undies, adorned with great, big heart patterns on them." Mitra giggles, the sound complimenting the playing of Agnimitra’s gittern rather smoothly. [pc.isDK |Although you know it’s all for Mitra’s benefit, the story is a bit too fantastic and childish for you. You wonder what the real story is – and you wonder which parts of Agnimitra’s retelling is being censored. |While it’s a bit on the childish end, you can’t help but at least smile a bit at the enthusiastic-but-censored retelling, especially given how much Mitra is enjoying it. Some of the other adult harpies laugh right alongside her. If nothing else, Agnimitra knows how to keep her audience laughing. ] "He was so embarrassed, he and his men fled the cave, but not before I made them promise never to return, and to stop their dastardly thieving ways. Since then, and this is true – well, it’s all true, but this is especially true – the bandit problems of that area of Tronarii were put to a swift and sudden end. When I got Luqetza out of her cage, the first thing she did was give me a kiss on the cheek." With one last brush of her fingers on the gittern’s by-now worn strings, she lifts her hand high and gives an elongated bow to her audience. "And that is why they call my Agnimitra, the Fiercest of the Harpies," she concludes. "I single-handedly cleared a cave of its bandit infestation, while saving my wife and daughter from their evil, underhanded clutches. My prowess as a fighter is known far and wide, from Tronarii, to Izkanti, all the way here to the Frost Marches. My skills with a blade are unmatched, after all this time!" Mitra rests on her knees, looking up at Agnimitra with wide, glittering eyes. "Woooooooow," she sighs in wonder as she reruns the whole theatre play in her mind’s eye over and over. "Did all of that really happen, great-grandma Agni?" "Yep, it all really happened," Agnimitra replies – perhaps a bit too quickly. [pc.isBimbo |It gives you a kind of vibe that you’re not sure you understand. You don’t think Agnimitra is lying... but you don’t think she’s telling the truth. But you can at least tell that she’s telling a dumbed-down version of the story for Mitra. Maybe you could ask Agnimitra to tell the uncensored story if Mitra’s not here – say, when she’s gone to bed, late at night...? |You can tell that she’s lying through omission. The basics of the story are accurate, but... the whole thing is far too, well, silly, to be an accurate retelling. If you want to know the real story, you’ll have to ask again when Mitra isn’t present. Like, say, when Mitra’s gone to bed, late at night... ] |Rather than damage her instrument, she lifts it off her lap and stands it upright on her thigh, looking it over like it was both a piece of art, but something she had seen a hundred times before and it no longer spoke to her like it did the first time. She lets out another heavy sigh through her nose before she lies it down beside her. "My fingers are starting to hurt," she says, smiling weakly to the other harpies. Some of them give a light, well-meaning laugh in response. "Luqezta, Torkelie and I were on the road between cities. It was the twilight hours; the sun had sunk over the sand dunes and the sky was bright orange on one side and light-purple on the other." Her lips curl inward for a moment to wet them, then she takes another sigh. "I was shot in the neck with an arrow. Died instantly. I have no idea what happened after that." [pc.isDK |The other girls in the room gasp at the suddenness of the news. You remain stone-faced: you saw firsthand Agnimitra’s ability to resurrect. Her dying and coming back isn’t shocking news to you. |You and each of the harpies in the room gasp at the suddenness of the news. You’ve seen firsthand Agnimitra’s ability to resurrect, but... well, just, the thought of how gruesome some of her deaths could be never crossed your mind. ] "The desert gets pretty hot during the day, so, it only took a day or two for me to resurrect right where they got me," she continues. "The first thing I saw when I came back was the blood on the sand, dried and mostly covered – just streaks of it along the road, half-buried under the billowing sands. There wasn’t a lot. You’d think it was just a little accident, something someone could walk off." "I flew to the nearest settlement, quick as I could, and started asking if anyone had seen any harpies with rainbow-colored plumage lately. It was their most defining feature. They would have stood out in the crowds really well. And yeah, I got an answer," she continues. She rolls her head to one side as her tongue presses out from the inside of her cheek. "There was a stall in the local bazaar that was selling bracelets and necklaces that had rainbow feathers on them. So I go to the guy, and I ask him where he got them, and he gives me some noise about ‘trade secrets,’ so I make a scene. Reached over the counter, grabbed him by the face, started getting real hot. I ask him again. He’s much more willing to talk, suddenly." [pc.isDK |Fuck yeah, now you’re getting to the good stuff. You knew you kept Agnimitra around for a reason. |You’ve seen Agnimitra weaponize her abilities as a phoenix in combat, but, well, the circumstances are different. If Agnimitra really wanted to, if she really wanted to hurt her opponents... you wonder what her limits, personal or otherwise, would be. ] "There’s a group of bandits in the area that called themselves the Hundred Dead Men. The number was actually sixty-two," she says with a smarmy, crooked grin. It’s not meant to be a joke, and the story’s not meant to be funny. "Ran by a guy that called himself Essache – the word meant ‘shepherd to the forgotten,’ back in the day. They had been terrorizing western Tronarii for a while. They were muggers. I wasn’t afraid of getting personal with some muggers, but I didn’t expect them to take me out from a distance. They knew who I was." "It wasn’t hard to find a Dead Man later that night. I trailed him back to their hideout in the wastes, some cave way off the beaten path. I walk in, and I find Essache–" She stops. Her brow furrows and she’s forced to look away as her eyes shut tight. She takes another long, deep, stuttering sigh through her nose as she tries to steel herself for the rest of her story. "It’s been more years than I’ve bothered to count, and, you know... I try to focus on the better memories that I had with Luqetza and our daughter Torkelie. Every family I’ve had has had their low points, but I remember them for their high points and who they are." Her knuckles turn white as she grips onto the edge of the table she’s sitting on. "This one particular memory never got any easier to bring up." "You don’t have to," one of the harpy women suggests. As soon as she does, the others fidget. That was the wrong thing to say – of course Agnimitra knew that. "What, and stop just before the ‘fiercest of the harpies’ part?" she asks, the corners of her mouth turning upward. "There’s an important lesson to be learned about your great-grandma Agni in this story, you know." She lifts her thumb to her nose and brushes it against her nostrils, wiping something away. "So, I walk into the den of the Hundred Dead Men, and there’s Essache. He’s easy to spot. Not because he was big, or tall, or sat on a throne. It was because he was wearing Luqetza’s feathers. The whole fff–" She stops, letting her teeth sit on her lips. "All of them. Everything but her hair, from the neck down. I walked into that cave and I saw a s-strange man wearing my wife’s feathers like a coat." "So I burnt it all. Everything in that cave. Every single thing." She lifts her eyes and scans them across her audience, starting with you and meeting the eyes of every other adult sequentially. "I remember starting, and I remember finishing, but I don’t remember anything in between. When I left that cave, I was covered in stab wounds – I don’t remember how they got there. My clothes were white going in, and they, uh, weren’t, coming out." She continues without skipping a beat, at this point trying to get through the story quickly. "I pulled every body from that cave and left them in the desert sun within eyesight of the road. They’d all been burnt smooth; I couldn’t tell them apart, whether one was a guy or a girl, or which one was Essache. It didn’t matter anymore. I pulled sixty-two of the Hundred Dead Men from that cave." She shrugs her shoulders. "No idea what happened to the other thirty-eight. I sat on top of a dune overlooking the pile of bodies until I bled out. It took a few days. I wanted everyone to know that I did it." "When you hear the phrase ‘Fiercest of the Harpies,’ you probably thought of my skill as a fighter, right?" she asks rhetorically. None of the harpies in her audience answer either way. "That’s what I was going for. I didn’t want people calling me ‘the Most Violent of the Harpies’ or ‘Agnimitra the War Criminal’. And I didn’t go out of my way to write a song about how I..." She leans back and takes another sigh through her nose. As she does, her fingers brush the neck of her gittern; she turns to look at it and wraps her fingers around its neck, bringing it back to her lap. "It was Luqetza that encouraged me to keep playing the gittern, you know," she says as she gives the strings another strum. "I didn’t play an instrument before I met her. She could play the lyre like an angel; the most talent I had at the time was beating drums like an ape." She laughs – a real, genuine giggle that brings an earnest smile to her lips. "She thought it’d be cute if we could duet someday." ] [var0 |Agnimitra flicks her wrist, flinging the discomfort from her fingers after all of that hard gittern playing. "Phew!" she says. "Man, that story really took a lot out of me. Does anyone have any other requests?" She smiles wryly, but it doesn’t meet her eyes. "Maybe something a little easier on the fingers?" |Agnimitra looks down at the gittern, letting her fingernails rest against the strings of the instrument. "Playing always helps me think of her and Torkelie. And thinking of them always helps me calm down." She purses her lips and inhales deeply through her nose as she pulls her head back. After holding it in her chest for a moment, she brings her head back down. "I could go for another request." A thick silence drapes over the other harpies in the room. "Are you sure?" one of them asks. "I mean..." "I don’t want to leave my concert on a note like that one," she answers. "All of my other titles have, uh, better stories to them. And actual songs that I memorized. I don’t want the last story that I tell here be about the heinous things I’m capable of. And besides: you never let the audience leave on a worse note than they came in." It’s a weird logic, but... you can understand it. ]'

rows.original:
Your walk through the fortress is interrupted by a familiar harpy with red plumage. Although... it’s particular that that doesn’t describe just one woman anymore.
    
    "Oh!" Zhara says, jolting upright once she sees you out of the corner of your eye. She quickly steps up to you, but not so close as to get into your personal space. "Hey, [zhara.isMom
        |lover
        |Boss
    ]!"
    
    [dayNight
        |You ask her what she’s doing in the fort. Didn’t you give her something to do if she wants to keep living here?
        
        "Well, okay, calm your tits," she says, smirking as she leans back. "As it happens, I had busted a shoulder strap for my pauldron, and I came in for a spare. Literally in-and-out." She rotates her shoulder, where her pauldron sits, good as new. You suppose your question could have come off as unintentionally interrogative.
        |You suppose it’s not a surprise to see her in the Wayfort at this hour. Her work for the day must be completed.
        
        "Pssh, as if you even need to ask," she says, lifting her nose up at you and giving you a smarmy smile. "[wayfort.harpiesTGN
            |The girls and I were already professional lawbreakers before you told us to do it for real. Your coffers are good and fat after today’s work, I can guarantee that!
            |Turns out it’s real easy to intimidate undesirables off your property when you have a gang of flying, screeching harpies circling above them the second they roll onto our turf. The wayfort’s never been safer! Unless the girls and I don’t like you, of course.
        ]"
    ]
    
    "But while I’m here, I’ve been meaning to ask you something," she continues. "Now that I know that you know Great-Grandma Agni, I was hoping I could take tomorrow off so I could fly home to the Peaks and get something of hers. She told me to hang onto it and to give it back when we was reborn, but, well, knowing her, I wouldn’t be surprised if she forgot."
    
    Zhara is asking you for a day off so she can get something that once belonged to Agnimitra. You ask her what her contingency is for her crew, since their leader wouldn’t be here if you grant it.
    
    "I got a second-in-command. She knows the ropes well enough to run the gig without my harping over her shoulder. Don’t worry about it, Boss, [zhara.isMom
        |you don’t just keep me around for my chicken thighs," she snickers
        |I’m more than just a pretty face and some dumb muscle. At least one of my muscles is pretty smart," she snickers
    ].
    
    Zhara seems confident that her crew will be able to function without her for twenty-four hours. For all intents and purposes, things shouldn’t change while she’s missing. It just comes down to whether you’ll allow her that time off.
rows.translation:
你在要塞中行走时，一个熟悉的红羽鹰身女妖打断了你的脚步。不过……如今这番描述已经不只适用于一个女人了。
    
    “哦！”扎菈从眼角发现你，顿时挺直身体。她迅速迎上前来，却没有靠得太近、侵犯你的私人空间。“嘿，[zhara.isMom
        |亲爱的
        |老大
    ]！”
    
    [dayNight
        |你问她来要塞里做什么。想继续住在这里的话，你不是给她安排过工作吗？
        
        “好吧，冷静点，”她向后仰身坏笑着说道。“其实，我肩甲的一条肩带断了，所以进来取根备用的。我真的拿完就走。”她转动肩膀；那里的肩甲已经焕然一新。你想，刚才的问题也许无意间听起来像在审问她。
        |这个时间在驿堡里看到她并不奇怪。她今天的工作应该已经结束了。
        
        “嘁，这还用问吗，”她冲你抬起鼻子，露出自鸣得意的笑容。“[wayfort.harpiesTGN
            |在你叫我们正式干这行之前，我和姑娘们就已经是职业罪犯了。我敢保证，今天干完活以后，你的金库又肥又满！
            |事实证明，不受欢迎的家伙刚踏进我们的地盘，一群会飞、会尖叫的鹰身女妖便在头顶盘旋；想把他们吓走简直轻而易举。驿堡从来没有这么安全过！当然，除非我和姑娘们不喜欢你。
        ]”
    ]
    
    “不过既然我来了，正好有件事一直想问你，”她继续说道。“现在我知道你认识阿格尼曾祖母了，所以想请明天一天假，飞回群峰去取她的一件东西。她叫我替她保管，等她转世后再还给她；不过嘛，以我对她的了解，她就算忘了我也不会惊讶。”
    
    扎菈想请一天假，去取一件曾属于阿格尼米特拉的东西。你问她为手下安排了什么后备方案；毕竟，准假以后，她们的首领就不在这里了。
    
    “我有个副手。她对这套活足够熟悉，就算我不在旁边唠叨，也能把事情办好。别担心，老大，[zhara.isMom
        |你留我在身边又不只是为了这对鸡腿，”她窃笑道
        |我不只有一张漂亮脸蛋和一身傻力气。至少有一块肌肉还算聪明，”她窃笑道
    ]。
    
    扎菈相信，即使自己离开二十四小时，手下仍能正常运作。无论从哪方面看，她不在期间也不会发生什么变化。现在只看你愿不愿意批准她休假。

rows.original:
Hell, Zhara’s reassured you that she has things under control, and you don’t have any reason not to believe her[pc.isDK
            |
            |. That, and everyone deserves a break now and again
        ]. Sure, she can take the day off tomorrow.
        
        "Awesome," she cheers, [zhara.isMom
            |stepping into you to kiss you on the cheek
            |pumping her fist in victory
        ]. "Thanks, [pc.name]. I’m really excited to see Great-Grandma Agni’s reaction to her present."
        
        She pulls away from you. [dayNight
            |"But in the meantime, I should get back to work. Gotta earn my hours off, and all." She spreads her wings as she approaches the nearest window large enough for her to leap out of. "[wayfort.harpiesTGN
                |That money isn’t going to liberate itself!
                |Someone’s gotta keep those ‘undesirables’ off our turf!
            ]"
            
            With a leap, she’s out the window and disappeared into the daylight.
            |"I’ll leave first thing in the morning. But in the meantime, the night’s still young." She turns around and begins to walk away, putting far more effort into the sway of her gait than is necessary. Naturally, your eyes are drawn to her shapely legs and the upward swell of her rear end. "If you want me to work a little harder to earn a few more hours off, well... you know where to find me."
            
            She gives you one last look over her shoulder before vanishing around the corner, disappearing deeper into the wayfort.
        ]
rows.translation:
见鬼，扎拉已经向你保证她能把一切都控制好，你没有任何理由不相信她。[pc.isDK
            |
            |。 而且，每个人都该偶尔休息一下
        ]。当然，她明天可以请一天假。
        
        “太好了，”她高兴地叫道，[zhara.isMom
            |凑近你，轻吻你的脸颊
            |兴奋地挥舞着拳头庆祝胜利
        ]。“谢谢，[pc.name]。我真的很期待看到曾祖母阿格尼收到礼物后的反应。”
        
        她从你身边退开。[dayNight
            |“不过现在，我得回去上班了。总得把休假的时间挣出来嘛。”她展开翅膀，朝最近那扇大得足以让她跳出去的窗户走去。“[wayfort.harpiesTGN
                |那些钱是不会自己主动跑到你手里的！
                |总得有人把那些“不受欢迎的人”赶出我们的地盘才行！
            ]”
            
            她纵身一跃，翻出窗外，消失在阳光之中。
            |“我明天一早就走。不过现在，夜晚还长着呢。”她转过身，开始走开，走路时腰肢摇摆的幅度远比实际需要的要大。自然而然地，你的目光被她那优美的双腿以及臀部向上隆起的曲线吸引住了。“如果你想让我再努力一点，好多挣几个小时的假，那么……你知道上哪儿找我。”
            
            她最后回头看了你一眼，随即拐过转角，消失在驿堡深处。
        ]

rows.original:
After taking a moment to consider it, you tell her that, no, you’d prefer it if she stays here, at least for a bit. You’ll keep her request for time off in the back of your head and assure her that it’s not a hard ‘no’; it’s a ‘ask me again later’.
        
        Zhara seems taken aback, honestly surprised that you’d deny her request for time off. "Really?" she asks. "Even if it meant getting something for Gre – for Agnimitra?"
        
        Again, you just want her here for a bit. You’ll grant her the leave she wants eventually.
        
        "Uh," she stutters, holding a long, droll note for a moment. "Okay. [dayNight
            |I, uh... better get back to work, then."
            
            She was clearly not expecting you to put up resistance like that, but, still, as her employer, she’s respecting your decision, which is nice. Without another word, she turns around and makes for the largest window, leaping out of it and resuming her duties to the fort.
            |I, uh... well, I’ll see you around, then."
            
            She was clearly not expecting you to put up resistance like that, but, still, as her employer, she’s respecting your decision, which is nice. Without another worse, she turns around and heads deeper into the fortress without giving you another look over her shoulder.
        ]
rows.translation:
经过片刻思考，你告诉她，不，你希望她能留在这里，至少再待一段时间。你会把她请假的请求记在心里，并向她保证，这不是一个坚决的“拒绝”，而是“等会儿再问我吧”。
        
        扎拉似乎有些惊讶，真的没想到你会拒绝她请假的请求。“真的吗？”她问道，“哪怕这意味着要给曾祖母——给阿格尼米特拉弄点什么？”
        
        你只是想让她暂时留在这里而已。最终，你会批准她想要的休假。
        
        “呃，”她结结巴巴地说，拖着一个长长的、滑稽的调子停了一会儿。“好吧。[dayNight
            |我，呃……那我还是回去工作吧。
            
            她显然没料到你会这样抵抗，不过，她仍然尊重你作为雇主的决定，这很不错。她没有再多说一句话，转身走向最大的那扇窗户，纵身跳了出去，继续履行她在堡垒中的职责。
            |我，呃……好吧，那回头见吧。”
            
            她显然没料到你会这样反抗，不过，她仍然尊重你作为雇主的决定，这很不错。她没有再说一个字，转身向堡垒深处走去，甚至没有回头看你一眼。
        ]

        |Zhara, by herself, wandering the halls with some expediency
        |Zhara, and beside her is Agnimitra. Zhara marches through the halls with some expediency
    ], looking into rooms for a second before dipping back out and resuming. From her hurried gait and her quick glances, she must be looking for someone or something.
    
    "Ah!" she says once she spots you. "[pc.name]! [party.has agni
        |And Great Granda Agni! Just the two people I was looking for!
        |Just the person we were looking for!
    ]"
    
    [party.has agni
        |You see that she’s back from her day off, looking no worse for wear. Although, you notice that she doesn’t have that gift that she was going on about with her.
        
        "Gift?" Agnimitra asks, tilting her head to one side. "Zhara was going to give you a gift[zhara.isMom
            |?" She glances down at Zhara’s stomach for a moment. "Is it another baby
        ]?"
        
        [zhara.isMom
            |Ignoring Agnimitra’s question, 
        ]Zhara grabs you both by the wrist and gives you a pull. "Follow me to the living quarters," she says. "I wasn’t gonna just lug the whole thing around the fort until I found the two people I wanted to show it to."
        |You can see that Zhara’s back from her day off – but she had promised that whatever she went to her ‘roost’ for was a gift for Agnimitra. Has she given it to her already?

rows.original: "Okay," Zhara says once she gets you and Agnimitra to her bed. She spins around to face you both with a big, toothy, giddy grin on her lips. Zhara glances between you both a few times, trying to plan out how she wants to do this in her head. "Okay," she says again, reaching up to place her hands on Agnimitra’s shoulders. "Great Granda Agni, you stand here, and [pc.name], you stand... here, beside her." She guides Agnimitra to stand a few paces from the foot of Zhara’s bunk, with you to her right, as Zhara turns towards her bed. You and Agnimitra exchange glances, and she gives you an unusually warm smile – like Zhara is four years old again and she’s trying to impress her grandma with something she made. Although they look roughly the same age, Zhara will always be Agnimitra’s great-granddaughter, in that way. You idly wonder if Zhara’s mother would ever act this way around Agnimitra again. "Okay," Zhara says again, hefting a small trunk from underneath her bunk and lying it flat on the bed. It’s about the size and depth of her torso, and from the motion of her arm, it’s not especially heavy. Whatever’s in there is somewhat large, but light. "Great-Grandma," she starts, "I don’t know if you remember this, but way back, waaaaaaay back, when you were, uh..." She pauses. "Older? Than you are now?" "I get it," Agnimitra says with a laugh. "Well, way back, you gave me this, and you told me to hang onto it for you. You said that you’d forget about it if you didn’t." Agnimitra still has that warm smile on her face, but it’s frozen: she has no idea what it is Zhara’s talking about. "Uh, yeah, I’ll be honest: I had it right back then, because I don’t remember this," she admits with a shrug. "But then, I don’t remember what I had for breakfast." "That’s okay," Zhara continues. "You said that it’d come back to you once you saw it." She steps away from the bed, inviting Agnimitra to open the trunk. Her fingers go to the two simple latches keeping it shut, and she flings it open– And inside is... clothes. Clothes with darker colors: mostly blacks, with some off-yellow for highlights. Agnimitra runs her hands over the material – whatever it is, it’s tough, like cotton, but it’s smooth like silk. And there’s a whole lot more of it than the clothing she’s wearing now: just three red capes sewn together. Agnimitra’s face scrunches, with her brow furrowing and her nostrils flaring. She doesn’t recognize it. "Did, uh, I happen to give you any hints?" she asks Zhara, half-sarcastically. At that, Zhara hesitates. She glances to you as if you’d have a better answer, then lowers her head. "No," she replies. "You said you’d remember it." "Hmm." Agnimitra hooks her fingers underneath the clothing and lifts it up. She presses her thumb underneath its fold, and lets the rest of it unfurl. It’s a dress top, with no sleeves, and the hem having been cut into halves so that the material reaches down her sides, but leaves her midriff and back exposed. Between the holes for the arms is a long, thick strap, likely meant to be a sewn-in bra. What draws your eyes is the yellow highlights down the hem of the fabric, sewn in jagged lines from the outside in, looking almost like thunderbolts. An unusual piece already, but what really sets it apart from a typical shirt is that is has a number of metal beads rimming the holes of the sleeves, culminating in a pair of spikes at the top of the arm loops. It’d look more in-place as some kind of orcish combat outfit, something that’s meant to be worn on a battlefield, but it doesn’t provide nearly enough protection to be useful for combat. Although you suppose it could look intimidating from a distance. Agnimitra gasps, jolting in place. "Wait," she says. She tosses the top onto the bed beside the trunk and pulls out the second half of the piece inside it. When it unfurls, it’s a long pair of pants with a similar color scheme: mostly black, but with sharp, punctuating yellow highlights, provoking power and noise against the comparative listless silence of the ensemble. Similar to the top, it has metal insets all along the outside of the pantlegs, going from the waistband to the ankles. Unlike the top, though, the pants have too much fabric: long, flowing tassels extend at different parts of the legs before ending at the ankles, seemingly sewn on for no reason at all. Other than to look cool in a billowing wind, maybe. "Aw, no way!" Agnimitra says, jumping on the spot as she looks the pants over. "I was just thinking about these the other day!" Zhara brightens up as Agnimitra does. "So you remember them?" "Yeah! I was wondering where I put them!" She lowers the pants and brings it to her waist to test their length. The ankles just barely touch the floor, a discrepancy that’ll be adjusted for once she puts them on. "They’ll still fit! Gods, a whole generation later, and my body hasn’t changed an inch!" You try to picture Agnimitra in that clothing. While it would cover her up more than the three capes sewn together, it wouldn’t be by much, especially in the top. And the blacks and yellows would clash with the red of her feathers (or perhaps ‘contrast’ is a better word). It would require a certain... attitude to pull off a look like that, especially with her natural colors. Zhara steps forward, bending around the corner of her bunk to try and get a better look at the raiment. "What makes these clothes so special?" she asks. "Like, are they your favorite, or something?" "Now that’s a story!" Agnimitra says, raising her index finger and leaving her mouth open as if she had something else to say. She freezes for a moment. "That’s I’ve mostly forgotten. Mostly! I still remember some of it." She sets the pants down and picks the shirt back up, lifting it up to her neck. Like the pants, the fabric extends a bit too far down, but it’ll fill out when she puts it on. "You’re familiar with the legend of the Sorran Adjudicators, right?" "Yeah," Zhara answers. You interrupt: you’re not. "Well, Sorra is the patron of winged creatures, right?" Zhara explains. "She’s all about the good stuff about being able to fly. The freedom to go anywhere; the sky is to us as the land is to you, and all that. But she’s not all smiles and happiness and, well, she can be a bad bitch when you piss her off. Long story short, the Sorran Adjudicators are Sorra’s personal attack dogs. Sorta like what the Astrida are for Nareva, if you’re familiar with them at all. Sorra’s got clerics and witches and all, but the Adjudicators, they were her best of the best." "And this is their uniform!" Agnimitra says, flapping the shirt in front of you. Which causes Zhara to reel back in surprise – she didn’t know that. "They’re a myth!" Zhara exclaims. "They’re a bedtime story you tell little kids to give them something to aspire to!" "Zhara, darling," Agnimitra says, curling her mouth into a wide-but-modestly-insincere smile. "Your great-grandma is immortal. Is it such a surprise that there’s some truth to the occasional myth and legend?" "What, are you on a first-name basis with god?" Agnimitra tilts her head. "Isn’t everyone?" she asks. "I don’t think Sorra has more than one name. Anyway!" She turns and lifts the top away from her, spreading out the fabric to get a better look at it. "This is more than just a fashion statement. It might not look it, but these are holy, blessed artifacts – anyone that wears them is blessed with the power of Sorra. I’m an immortal phoenix." She snaps her fingers, and her thumb alights, wreathed in flame down to her knuckle. "But imagine if I put these on, and then I shot lightning from my fingertips instead?" Wait, you’d like to back up a second. She’s holding the raiments of Sorra’s blessed warriors? And they’re perfectly tailored to Agnimitra’s body? Was she ever going to tell you on her own time that she was once one of Sorra’s holy knights? "Just as soon as I remembered," she says with a snicker. "Not a lot of room to spare upstairs." Even if that’s true, it’s hard to imagine Agnimitra as, well, someone’s typical idea of a ‘warrior’. What sort of role specifically did she have in the Adjudicators? Did she just fling around fire and lightning? "I whipped around a big ol’ axe," she says with a laugh. She lifts her arm and flexes her bicep. It doesn’t rise very high. "But, you know, there is such an occupation as a ‘warrior bard’. Although that wasn’t distinctive enough for us back then, so, we called me the team’s ‘Storm Skald’. And it’s true: my arms aren’t as big and beefy as, say, [pc.strengthRange 0 75 |a minotaurs |yours, [pc.name] ], but being able to rally the troops and get them ready for battle was as an important duty as healing wounds, or directing the troops, or... well, swinging around a big axe." The air goes silent between you three for a moment. "Can I wear them?" Zhara asks. "We’re shaped the same. They’d probably fit me." Agnimitra scratches at her chin as she considers it. A fake smile crosses her lips, looking like she’s about to try and sell Zhara some snake oil. "Do I want to give a young, twenty-something leader of a bandit group a holy artifact that would bestow upon her the powers of one of the Seven?" she asks in turn. "Oh, come on! I’m dependable, I can be trusted with them! How old were you when Sorra gave them to you?" "Oh, now that’s a question." Agnimitra closes one eye as she thinks about it. "I would have needed to be young and strong enough to perform my physical tasks as an Adjudicator, so, physically, not much older than you, Zhara. But literally? I would have been..." She pauses, purses her lips, balloons her cheeks. She lets out a long, steady exhale as she tries to put a number to her thoughts. "In my mid-hundreds? It would have been a long time ago." Zhara flicks her wrist dismissively as she turns away. "Whatever, grandma." Agnimitra snickers. "In any case, thank you for bringing these back to me," she says, stepping forward and hugging Zhara around the shoulders. Zhara initially doesn’t reciprocate, spurned from not being allowed to wear the raiments, but she eventually relents – she loves her great-grandma. "Gimme a few hours so I can model them for you two." A few hours? For a change of clothes? "Oh, no, I can just slip on the clothes," she says as she sets the top down onto the bed beside the trunk. "But if you want me to do this right, I need a bit of extra prep time." With both her hands free, she places one on Zhara’s collarbone and the other on yours – and, suddenly, she starts pushing you towards the door to the living quarters. "Both of you, out! Out, out! I need space to work my magic!" You never knew Agnimitra to be so insistent! As soon as she saw those clothes, it’s like she became a totally different person. Perhaps clothes really do make the woman.
rows.translation: 好了，”扎拉把你们俩带到她的床边后说道。她转过身来，脸上挂着灿烂而略带傻气的笑容，看着你们俩。“好了，”她又重复了一遍，然后伸手将手放在阿格尼米特拉的肩上。“伟大的阿格尼爷爷，您就站在这里吧[pc.name]，你站在……这里，她的旁边。” 她引导阿格尼米特拉站在扎拉床铺的脚边几步远的地方，让你站在她的右边，此时扎拉正转向她的床铺。你和阿格尼米特拉交换了一个眼神，而她给了你一个异常温暖的微笑——就好像扎拉又回到了四岁的时候，正在试图用自己制作的东西来给奶奶留下好印象一样。虽然她们看起来年纪相仿，但从某种意义上来说，扎拉永远都是阿格尼米特拉的曾孙女。你不禁会想，扎拉的母亲是否还会再以这样的方式对待阿格尼米特拉。 好吧，”扎拉再次说道，她从床铺下方拿出了一个小型箱子，将其平放在床上。这个箱子的大小和深度差不多与她的躯干相当，从她移动手臂的动作来看，这个箱子应该并不特别重。箱子里装的物品应该体积较大，但重量较轻。“曾祖母，”她开始说道，“我不知道您是否还记得这件事……很久很久以前，当您还……”她停顿了一下，“比现在年纪更大的时候？ 我明白了，”阿格尼米特拉笑着说。 “嗯，很久以前，你把这个给了我，还让我帮你保管好。你说如果我不留着的话，你就会把它忘掉。” 阿格尼米特拉的脸上依然挂着温暖的笑容，但那笑容已经凝固了——她完全不明白扎拉在说什么。“呃，说实话，我当时确实留着它，因为我根本不记得这件事了，”她耸了耸肩承认道，“不过后来，我甚至都不记得自己早餐吃了什么了。 没关系，”扎拉继续说道，“你说过，只要看到了它，它就会回到你身边。” 她从床边走开，示意阿格尼米特拉去打开那个箱子。她的手指触到了固定箱子的两个简单锁扣，然后猛地将其拉开—— 里面装的是……衣服。颜色较深的衣服：主要是黑色，还有一些淡黄色的元素作为点缀。阿格尼米特拉用手触摸这种材料——不管它到底是什么，它的质地很坚韧，像棉花一样，但表面却像丝绸一样光滑。而且，这种材料的数量远远超过了她现在身上穿的这些衣服：她现在穿的这些衣服只不过是三块红色斗篷拼接在一起而已。 阿格尼米特拉的眉头紧锁，鼻孔也微微张开，她显然没有认出那个东西。“我，呃，有没有给你什么提示呢？”她半带讽刺地问扎拉。 听到这个问题，扎拉犹豫了一下。她瞥了你一眼，似乎觉得你应该能给出更好的答案，然后低下了头：“没有，”她回答道，“你说你会记得的。 嗯。” 阿格尼米特拉将手指伸到她的衣服下面，将其掀了起来。她用拇指按住衣服的褶皱处，然后让其余部分慢慢展开。那是一件没有袖子的连衣裙，下摆被剪成了两半，这样布料就会垂到她的两侧，但她的腹部和背部却暴露在外。在用于固定手臂的那些孔洞之间，有一条长而粗的带子，很可能是用来固定胸罩的。真正吸引你注意的是布料下摆处那些黄色的装饰线条——它们是以不规则的线条从外向内缝制而成的，看起来简直就像闪电一样。 这件衣服本身就已经很不寻常了，但真正让它区别于普通衬衫的地方在于，袖子上的孔洞周围镶嵌着许多金属珠子，而这些珠子在袖口处汇聚成一对尖刺。这种设计看起来更像是一种兽人战斗服装，是专为战场设计的，但实际上它所提供的保护远远不足以用于实战。不过，从远处看，这种设计确实会给人一种威慑感。 阿格尼米特拉倒吸一口凉气，猛地站住了。“等等，”她说。她把上衣扔到床边，然后从箱子里取出那条裤子的下半部分。当它被展开时，原来是一条颜色搭配相似的长裤：整体以黑色为主，但上面点缀着醒目的黄色条纹，这些鲜艳的色彩在整体沉闷的色调中显得格外醒目，仿佛在诉说着力量与活力。与上衣类似，这条裤子的裤腿外侧也装有金属装饰条，这些装饰条从腰带一直延伸到脚踝。不过，与上衣不同的是，这条裤子的金属装饰条数量更多。很多这种裤子的设计十分独特：长而飘逸的流苏分布在裤腿的各个部位，最终延伸至脚踝处，看起来仿佛是毫无缘由地被缝上去的。当然，除了在微风中摆动时显得格外酷炫之外，大概也没有其他作用了吧。 “啊，不可能！”阿格尼米特拉边说边跳着脚查看这条裤子，“我刚才只是前几天我还在想这些呢！” 扎拉和阿格尼米特拉一样，脸上露出了笑容。“原来你还记得它们？” “当然记得！我一直在想把它们放在哪里呢！”她把裤子往下拉，拉到腰部，用来测试它们的长度是否合适。脚踝刚刚能够触到地面，这个尺寸上的差异等她穿上这些衣服后就会得到调整。“它们还是合适的！天啊，整整一代人过去了，可我的身体却一点都没有变化！” 你试着想象阿格尼米特拉穿上这些衣服的样子。虽然这件衣物覆盖她的面积比三件缝在一起的外套要大一些，但差距仍然不大，尤其是在上半身部分。而且黑色和黄色的搭配会与她羽毛上的红色形成对比……或者，用“形成鲜明反差”来形容可能更为准确。要做出那样的装扮，确实需要某种特定的……态度，尤其是考虑到她的自然肤色。 扎拉走上前，绕过床铺的角落，试图更仔细地看看那套服装。为什么这些衣服这么特别呢？”她问道，“难道它们是你最喜欢的衣服，还是有什么特别的原因吗？” “现在那就是一个故事啊！”阿格尼米特拉说着，抬起食指，张大嘴巴，似乎还想继续说些什么。她停顿了一下，“其实大部分内容我都已经忘记了。大部分吧！不过还是记得一些的。”她放下裤子，重新拿起衬衫，把它拉到脖子上。就像这条裤子一样，布料的下摆确实有点太长了，但等她穿上之后，就会显得合身了。“你应该听说过索拉信徒裁判者的传说吧？” “听说过，”扎拉回答道。 你插话道：其实你并不了解这个传说吧。 嗯，索拉毕竟是飞禽的守护者，对吧？”扎拉解释道，“她代表着飞行带来的种种好处——能够自由地飞往任何地方，对咱们来说，天空就如同陆地对你们一样重要。但是，她并不总是那么温柔快乐，当你惹她生气的时候，她也会变得非常凶狠的。长话短说，索拉信徒审判官们其实是索拉的私人武装力量。如果你了解娜瑞瓦的阿斯特里达的话，他们就可以理解为类似的角色。索拉虽然也有牧师和女巫之类的手下，但这些审判官们才是她最精锐的力量。这就是他们的制服！”阿格尼米特拉说着，在你面前晃动着那件衬衫。这一举动让扎拉惊讶得连连后退——她之前根本不知道这一点。那个那些都是神话罢了！”扎拉惊呼道，“那些不过是大人为了哄小孩子睡觉而编的故事，用来给他们树立一些奋斗目标罢了！” “扎拉，亲爱的，”阿格尼米特拉说道，她露出一个虽然灿烂却带着一丝虚伪的微笑，“你的曾祖母可是永生的。那么，偶尔出现的那些神话和传说中，有些内容确实是真实的，这有什么好奇怪的吗？” “什么？你和她已经熟到可以直呼其名的程度了？上帝阿格尼米特拉歪了歪头，问道：“难道不是所有人都是这样吗？”她接着说：“我觉得索拉应该只有一个名字吧。不管怎样！”她转过身，掀开了覆盖在布料上的东西，将布料摊开仔细端详起来。这不仅仅是一种时尚搭配。虽然看起来并不像，但这些其实是神圣的、受祝福的圣物——任何佩戴它们的人都会获得索拉的力量。我，就是一只不朽的凤凰。”她打了个响指，她的拇指上顿时燃起了火焰，一直蔓延到指关节处。但是想象一下，如果我戴上这些装备，然后开枪的话闪电而不是从我的指尖传递出去？” 等等，你先听我说清楚。她现在拿着索拉那些神圣战士的战袍？而这些战袍竟然完全适合阿格尼米特拉的身材？她之前难道不打算找个机会主动告诉你，她曾经也是索拉的神圣骑士之一吗？ 我刚想起来呢，”她带着一丝讥笑说道，“楼上的空间实在不够用。” 即便事实确实如此，也很难将阿格尼米特拉想象成人们心目中典型的“战士”形象。在裁决者组织中，她具体扮演了什么样的角色呢？她刚才真的是挥舞着火焰和闪电吗？ “我只是挥动了一把大斧头而已，”她笑着说道。她抬起手臂，展示了一下自己的二头肌，不过肌肉并没有明显地凸起。“不过，你也知道，确实有“战士吟游诗人”这样的职业。虽然在当时这还不够独特，因此我们给我起了个称呼——团队的“风暴吟游者”。事实上，我的手臂确实没有像某些人那样粗壮有力[pc.strengthRange 0 75 |牛头人 |你的，[pc.name] ]但是，能够集结军队并让他们做好战斗准备，这与治疗伤员、指挥军队一样，都是一项非常重要的职责……嗯，或者说，挥舞那把大斧头也同样重要。” 你们三个人之间的气氛在那一刻变得格外安静。 我可以穿它们吗？”扎拉问道，“我们的身材很相似，应该很合身吧。” 阿格尼米特拉挠了挠下巴，仔细考虑着这个问题。她的嘴角浮现出一丝假笑，看起来像是要试图向扎拉推销些什么“鬼把戏”似的。我究竟要不要把一件能赋予这位二十多岁的土匪头目‘七大强者’之一力量的神圣神器交给她呢？”她反问道。 “哦，别开玩笑了！我可是很可靠的人，把这样的神器交给我绝对没有问题！他们当时多大年纪？你当索拉把它们交给你的时候？” “哦，现在才想起来。那就是这是个问题……”阿格尼米特拉闭上一只眼睛，陷入沉思。“要担任裁判，我必须足够年轻且体力充沛，所以从身体条件上来说，我应该和你年纪相仿，扎拉。但按实际年龄来算的话……”她停顿了一下，抿紧嘴唇，鼓起脸颊，然后长长地呼出一口气，试图确定一个具体的年龄。“大概在几百岁左右吧？那应该是很久以前的事了。” 扎拉随意地甩了甩手腕，转身走开了：“算了，无所谓吧。奶奶阿格尼米特拉轻声笑了起来。“无论如何，还是谢谢你把这些东西还给我，”她说着，走上前，搂住了扎拉的肩膀。起初，扎拉并没有回应这个拥抱，因为之前她被禁止穿戴那些衣物；但最终她还是放松了——她爱她的曾祖母。给我几个小时，我就能为你们俩准备好这些衣服。” 几个小时？就为了换身衣服？ “哦，不，我可以直接穿上这些衣服就行了，”她说着，把上衣放在床边，靠近那个行李箱。但如果你们想让我把这件事做好，我就需要一些额外的准备时间。”她的双手都空出来了，一只手放在扎拉的锁骨上，另一只手放在你的手上——然后，她突然开始把你往生活区的门口推。“你们两个，出去！快出去！我需要空间施展我的魔法！”你从未见过阿格尼米特拉如此坚持己见。她一看到那些衣服，就好像完全变了一个人一样。 或许，衣服确实能改变一个女人。
rows.raw: ' "Okay," Zhara says once she gets you and Agnimitra to her bed. She spins around to face you both with a big, toothy, giddy grin on her lips. Zhara glances between you both a few times, trying to plan out how she wants to do this in her head. "Okay," she says again, reaching up to place her hands on Agnimitra’s shoulders. "Great Granda Agni, you stand here, and [pc.name], you stand... here, beside her." She guides Agnimitra to stand a few paces from the foot of Zhara’s bunk, with you to her right, as Zhara turns towards her bed. You and Agnimitra exchange glances, and she gives you an unusually warm smile – like Zhara is four years old again and she’s trying to impress her grandma with something she made. Although they look roughly the same age, Zhara will always be Agnimitra’s great-granddaughter, in that way. You idly wonder if Zhara’s mother would ever act this way around Agnimitra again. "Okay," Zhara says again, hefting a small trunk from underneath her bunk and lying it flat on the bed. It’s about the size and depth of her torso, and from the motion of her arm, it’s not especially heavy. Whatever’s in there is somewhat large, but light. "Great-Grandma," she starts, "I don’t know if you remember this, but way back, waaaaaaay back, when you were, uh..." She pauses. "Older? Than you are now?" "I get it," Agnimitra says with a laugh. "Well, way back, you gave me this, and you told me to hang onto it for you. You said that you’d forget about it if you didn’t." Agnimitra still has that warm smile on her face, but it’s frozen: she has no idea what it is Zhara’s talking about. "Uh, yeah, I’ll be honest: I had it right back then, because I don’t remember this," she admits with a shrug. "But then, I don’t remember what I had for breakfast." "That’s okay," Zhara continues. "You said that it’d come back to you once you saw it." She steps away from the bed, inviting Agnimitra to open the trunk. Her fingers go to the two simple latches keeping it shut, and she flings it open– And inside is... clothes. Clothes with darker colors: mostly blacks, with some off-yellow for highlights. Agnimitra runs her hands over the material – whatever it is, it’s tough, like cotton, but it’s smooth like silk. And there’s a whole lot more of it than the clothing she’s wearing now: just three red capes sewn together. Agnimitra’s face scrunches, with her brow furrowing and her nostrils flaring. She doesn’t recognize it. "Did, uh, I happen to give you any hints?" she asks Zhara, half-sarcastically. At that, Zhara hesitates. She glances to you as if you’d have a better answer, then lowers her head. "No," she replies. "You said you’d remember it." "Hmm." Agnimitra hooks her fingers underneath the clothing and lifts it up. She presses her thumb underneath its fold, and lets the rest of it unfurl. It’s a dress top, with no sleeves, and the hem having been cut into halves so that the material reaches down her sides, but leaves her midriff and back exposed. Between the holes for the arms is a long, thick strap, likely meant to be a sewn-in bra. What draws your eyes is the yellow highlights down the hem of the fabric, sewn in jagged lines from the outside in, looking almost like thunderbolts. An unusual piece already, but what really sets it apart from a typical shirt is that is has a number of metal beads rimming the holes of the sleeves, culminating in a pair of spikes at the top of the arm loops. It’d look more in-place as some kind of orcish combat outfit, something that’s meant to be worn on a battlefield, but it doesn’t provide nearly enough protection to be useful for combat. Although you suppose it could look intimidating from a distance. Agnimitra gasps, jolting in place. "Wait," she says. She tosses the top onto the bed beside the trunk and pulls out the second half of the piece inside it. When it unfurls, it’s a long pair of pants with a similar color scheme: mostly black, but with sharp, punctuating yellow highlights, provoking power and noise against the comparative listless silence of the ensemble. Similar to the top, it has metal insets all along the outside of the pantlegs, going from the waistband to the ankles. Unlike the top, though, the pants have too much fabric: long, flowing tassels extend at different parts of the legs before ending at the ankles, seemingly sewn on for no reason at all. Other than to look cool in a billowing wind, maybe. "Aw, no way!" Agnimitra says, jumping on the spot as she looks the pants over. "I was just thinking about these the other day!" Zhara brightens up as Agnimitra does. "So you remember them?" "Yeah! I was wondering where I put them!" She lowers the pants and brings it to her waist to test their length. The ankles just barely touch the floor, a discrepancy that’ll be adjusted for once she puts them on. "They’ll still fit! Gods, a whole generation later, and my body hasn’t changed an inch!" You try to picture Agnimitra in that clothing. While it would cover her up more than the three capes sewn together, it wouldn’t be by much, especially in the top. And the blacks and yellows would clash with the red of her feathers (or perhaps ‘contrast’ is a better word). It would require a certain... attitude to pull off a look like that, especially with her natural colors. Zhara steps forward, bending around the corner of her bunk to try and get a better look at the raiment. "What makes these clothes so special?" she asks. "Like, are they your favorite, or something?" "Now that’s a story!" Agnimitra says, raising her index finger and leaving her mouth open as if she had something else to say. She freezes for a moment. "That’s I’ve mostly forgotten. Mostly! I still remember some of it." She sets the pants down and picks the shirt back up, lifting it up to her neck. Like the pants, the fabric extends a bit too far down, but it’ll fill out when she puts it on. "You’re familiar with the legend of the Sorran Adjudicators, right?" "Yeah," Zhara answers. You interrupt: you’re not. "Well, Sorra is the patron of winged creatures, right?" Zhara explains. "She’s all about the good stuff about being able to fly. The freedom to go anywhere; the sky is to us as the land is to you, and all that. But she’s not all smiles and happiness and, well, she can be a bad bitch when you piss her off. Long story short, the Sorran Adjudicators are Sorra’s personal attack dogs. Sorta like what the Astrida are for Nareva, if you’re familiar with them at all. Sorra’s got clerics and witches and all, but the Adjudicators, they were her best of the best." "And this is their uniform!" Agnimitra says, flapping the shirt in front of you. Which causes Zhara to reel back in surprise – she didn’t know that. "They’re a myth!" Zhara exclaims. "They’re a bedtime story you tell little kids to give them something to aspire to!" "Zhara, darling," Agnimitra says, curling her mouth into a wide-but-modestly-insincere smile. "Your great-grandma is immortal. Is it such a surprise that there’s some truth to the occasional myth and legend?" "What, are you on a first-name basis with god?" Agnimitra tilts her head. "Isn’t everyone?" she asks. "I don’t think Sorra has more than one name. Anyway!" She turns and lifts the top away from her, spreading out the fabric to get a better look at it. "This is more than just a fashion statement. It might not look it, but these are holy, blessed artifacts – anyone that wears them is blessed with the power of Sorra. I’m an immortal phoenix." She snaps her fingers, and her thumb alights, wreathed in flame down to her knuckle. "But imagine if I put these on, and then I shot lightning from my fingertips instead?" Wait, you’d like to back up a second. She’s holding the raiments of Sorra’s blessed warriors? And they’re perfectly tailored to Agnimitra’s body? Was she ever going to tell you on her own time that she was once one of Sorra’s holy knights? "Just as soon as I remembered," she says with a snicker. "Not a lot of room to spare upstairs." Even if that’s true, it’s hard to imagine Agnimitra as, well, someone’s typical idea of a ‘warrior’. What sort of role specifically did she have in the Adjudicators? Did she just fling around fire and lightning? "I whipped around a big ol’ axe," she says with a laugh. She lifts her arm and flexes her bicep. It doesn’t rise very high. "But, you know, there is such an occupation as a ‘warrior bard’. Although that wasn’t distinctive enough for us back then, so, we called me the team’s ‘Storm Skald’. And it’s true: my arms aren’t as big and beefy as, say, [pc.strengthRange 0 75 |a minotaurs |yours, [pc.name] ], but being able to rally the troops and get them ready for battle was as an important duty as healing wounds, or directing the troops, or... well, swinging around a big axe." The air goes silent between you three for a moment. "Can I wear them?" Zhara asks. "We’re shaped the same. They’d probably fit me." Agnimitra scratches at her chin as she considers it. A fake smile crosses her lips, looking like she’s about to try and sell Zhara some snake oil. "Do I want to give a young, twenty-something leader of a bandit group a holy artifact that would bestow upon her the powers of one of the Seven?" she asks in turn. "Oh, come on! I’m dependable, I can be trusted with them! How old were you when Sorra gave them to you?" "Oh, now that’s a question." Agnimitra closes one eye as she thinks about it. "I would have needed to be young and strong enough to perform my physical tasks as an Adjudicator, so, physically, not much older than you, Zhara. But literally? I would have been..." She pauses, purses her lips, balloons her cheeks. She lets out a long, steady exhale as she tries to put a number to her thoughts. "In my mid-hundreds? It would have been a long time ago." Zhara flicks her wrist dismissively as she turns away. "Whatever, grandma." Agnimitra snickers. "In any case, thank you for bringing these back to me," she says, stepping forward and hugging Zhara around the shoulders. Zhara initially doesn’t reciprocate, spurned from not being allowed to wear the raiments, but she eventually relents – she loves her great-grandma. "Gimme a few hours so I can model them for you two." A few hours? For a change of clothes? "Oh, no, I can just slip on the clothes," she says as she sets the top down onto the bed beside the trunk. "But if you want me to do this right, I need a bit of extra prep time." With both her hands free, she places one on Zhara’s collarbone and the other on yours – and, suddenly, she starts pushing you towards the door to the living quarters. "Both of you, out! Out, out! I need space to work my magic!" You never knew Agnimitra to be so insistent! As soon as she saw those clothes, it’s like she became a totally different person. Perhaps clothes really do make the woman.'

rows.original: While you busy yourself with other tasks and oversights around the fort, Agnimitra pushing you from the quarters sits in the back of your mind, nagging at you to go back and see if she’s ready yet. Her being an immortal phoenix simply isn’t enough for her legacy: she’s also a holy knight, chosen by Sorra. [pc.isBimbo |Although you don’t blame her for forgetting. You tend to forget about things pretty quickly, too. |It boggles your mind how a fact like that just... slipped her mind, and it only came back to her when she saw her uniform. She’s been through a lot, but you’d have thought something like that would make an impression! ] You watch the [dayNight |sun’s movement through the sky |stars as they slowly shift through the night sky ] to keep passage of time. Agnimitra never comes to find you, and, eventually, your curiosity gets the better of you. Uninvited, you make your way back to the personal quarters in the fort – and as you approach, you, by coincidence, meet Zhara again, just outside the door. "You couldn’t handle the suspense either, huh?" she asks. You confirm. In fact, you’re still having a hard time wrapping your head around all of it. How does someone just forget that they have powerful holy artifacts in their possession? "Honestly, I’m not too surprised about that part," Zhara says with a laugh and a shrug. "Great-Grandma has always been kind of forgetful about stuff. I always wondered, you know, how she was before she was immortal – if she had an easier time remembering things." She steps into your space and turns away from the door. She leans her head forward, bringing her lips to your ear. "Between you and me," she whispers, "if I knew what those clothes were when she gave them to me, I definitely would have tried that shit on." That just proves her point – that Zhara probably couldn’t be trusted with powers like Sorra’s. Agnimitra gave her those clothes for safekeeping before you met either of them, and at that time, she still would have been a bandit leader, accosting strangers on the road for their money. "Oh, be real, [pc.name]," she says indignantly. "Would you not even give them a try if you had them?" [pc.corruptionRange 0 33 66 |If you knew that wearing clothes would bestow on you the power of storms and lightning? Honestly, probably not. That sounds like a lot of responsibility[silly |. Power always comes with it, after all ]. "Bah, you’re no fun." |You– Well... [var0 |They might fit you, but... No. No, it’s better not to think about it. The less you think about it, the less tempted you’ll be. "Sure, sure," Zhara says noncommittally. "But, like... what if, though, right?" ... Yeah, what if– No, you wouldn’t. And you ask Zhara to stop tempting you. She just laughs. |They wouldn’t fit you anyway. No need to even entertain the idea. "But what if they did?" They don’t, so you can stop fantasizing about it. The sooner the better. Zhara just laughs. ] |If you knew that the clothes you were holding would bestow upon you powers equal to one of the Seven’s[var0 |? And that they fit you ]? Hell yes, you’d wear them. You’d rock that shit twenty-four hours a day. The difference, you tell Zhara, is that you wouldn’t use them to bully some poor assholes just trying to cross the road. "What would you use them for, then?" Honestly? Something bigger than that. "Maybe it’s a good thing that neither of us have it, then," she says with a laugh. ] You push the door to the quarters open, hoping to move the conversation along before [pc.corruptionRange 0 66 |Zhara gets |you get ] too many more ideas on stealing a set of enchanted clothing. When you enter the room, it’s mostly empty – save for Agnimitra, having placed herself against a far wall, using a [wayfort.stateABC |shard of glass |a pane of glass |a mirror ] for her reflection. She’s facing away from you... but even from where you’re standing, the transformation is... intense. Her old clothing is set aside, resting on Zhara’s bed where the new raiments were, and Agnimitra is wearing the black-and-yellow outfit with the metal insets. Like she had promised, it fits her to a T, hugging her body without draping off it nor clinging to it. It has no sleeves and her back, and likely her midriff, are exposed. The pants fit her perfectly and reach down to her ankles, with the extra straps of material simply hanging limply off her legs, likely just meant to look cool. Next to her [wayfort.stateABC |makeup stand |glass pane |mirror ] is a greataxe: a massive, two-handed weapon with a double-sided head, capped with a glaive in between the bits. It looks modestly new: the metal doesn’t appear nicked from use, and the metal of the blades shine in the [dayNight |light of the streaming sun |din of the moonlight ]. Although it doesn’t look too big or heavy for Agnimitra to use, it would certainly be a change of pace compared to what you’re used to. She perks up and looks over her shoulder once she hears you approach. She’s wearing paint on her face, particularly across her eyes: setting them in a long, thick, dark streak of black that goes from ear to ear. It looks like some sort of war paint, at least from where you’re standing. "How long have you been standing there?" she asks. You respond that you just came in. "Oh." She turns back to her reflection to apply the finishing touches. "Damn, and I was looking forward to going out and meeting you like this. At least you only came in as I was finishing."
rows.translation: 当你忙于处理堡垒内的其他事务时，阿格尼米特拉从你的住处赶你离开的场景始终萦绕在脑海中，不断提醒你回去看看她是否已经准备好了。对她来说，仅仅作为一只不朽的凤凰远远不够——她还是索拉挑选出来的神圣骑士，她的传奇故事需要更多的内涵。 [pc.isBimbo |虽然你不会责怪她忘记这件事，但你自己也经常会很快就把事情忘掉吧。 |真让人难以理解，这样一个事实怎么就会从她的记忆中彻底消失呢？直到她看到了自己的制服，才想起来这件事。她经历了很多，但按常理来说，这样的事情应该会给她留下深刻的印象才对啊！ ] 你看着吧。 [dayNight |太阳在天空中的运动轨迹 |这些星星在夜空中缓缓移动，闪烁着光芒。 ]为了打发时间，你决定不再等待，也不去想阿格尼米特拉是否会来找你。最终，好奇心战胜了你的犹豫，你未经邀请，独自回到了堡垒里的个人住所。就在你接近门口的时候，巧合的是，你再次遇到了扎拉。 “你也是受不了这种悬念吧？”她问道。你点了点头。事实上，你至今仍然无法理解这一切究竟是怎么回事。一个人怎么可能忘记说实话，对于这一点我并不感到太惊讶，”扎拉笑着说，同时耸了耸肩。“我的曾祖母向来就是有点记性不好。我一直在想，你知道的，在她获得永生之前，她到底是怎样的一个人——她是否更容易记住各种事情呢。 她走进你的空间，然后转身背对大门。她把头凑过来，将嘴唇贴在你的耳边。跟你说实话吧，”她低声说道，“如果我知道她把那些衣服给我的时候，它们到底是什么来历的话，我当然我早就会那么做了。” 这恰恰证明了她的观点——像索拉那样的力量，恐怕不能交给扎拉来保管。在你们俩相遇之前，阿格尼米特拉把那些衣服交给她是为了让她妥善保管，而在那个时候，扎拉仍然只是一个强盗头目，在路上拦路抢劫陌生人的钱财罢了。 ]为了让她有时间思考。她现在正背对着你……但即便从你现在的位置来看，她身上的变化也确实非常明显。 她的旧衣服被放在了一边，放在了扎拉的床上，而那些新衣服则还在那里。阿格尼米特拉现在穿着那套黑白相间的衣服，衣服上还镶嵌着金属装饰。正如她所承诺的那样，这件衣服她穿得恰到好处，既不会松垂在身上，也不会紧贴身体。它没有袖子，因此她的后背，甚至可能是腹部，都暴露在外。这条裤子也非常合身，一直垂到她的脚踝处，而那些多余的布料带子只是松松地挂在她的腿上，大概只是为了增添一些时尚感罢了。
