rows.original: "I think we should find a nice spot on one of the further branches," Kiyoko tells you. "Not too close to the festivities so that we can be by ourselves, and yet not too far so that we can still see what's going on in the upper plaza. I think I know just the place." So it happens that you unpack your bundle at your fox-wife's discretion, using the cloth itself as a ground sheet for the two of you. Boxed food, a small collapsable wooden low table, plenty of boxed food, several bottles of strong rice liquor and the like — there's even a paper lantern made to be lit with foxfire. Clearly, they expect the festivities to stretch into the night. At least one of these each for over a hundred families — you can only wonder how long it took to prepare all this, and the number of hands that were involved. You knew foxes were fastidious, but the way even the food in the boxes from side dishes to whole meals is arranged is intended to evoke beauty and mindfulness — not inappropriate given what you understand of the event, but still. So much effort... [kiyoko.pregStage 1 |Digging through the other stuff in the package, Kiyoko fishes out a clay jar and gives it a dainty sniff. "Amazake. How thoughtful for the golden girl to provide my favorite." You reach out and poke your fox-wife's kit-filled belly, eliciting a giggle from her. It's not surprising; she can't have liquor when she's with child. "That's fine. Whether it's cherry blossoms in full bloom or delicious sake, none are a match for you, beloved. Going out with you would have been reason enough." She really knows how to flatter, doesn't she? Ah well, you can't expect a fox to have anything but a silver tongue... |Digging through the bottles, Kiyoko pulls out one of them and pops it open to give it a sniff. "I will say this for rural backwaters, too — the local flavors of liquor are always something. Not necessarily better, but more interesting; the sun, the soil, the rain, the breed of rice, the brewing process — back in the day, my mother would have them brought from all over the Old Country to our holdings. I do appreciate Komari using the local brew instead of importing; it gives the occasion a lot more meaning, I believe." Hmm... Kiyoko pours herself a cup, setting it out on the low folding table, then holds out the bottle to you. "Come, beloved. Have a cup as well." Well, don't mind if you do. You take up one of the small cups provided in the package and let Kiyoko pour you some, then down it as she does hers. The fire the strong rice liquor lights in your chest and stomach, with its slightly sweet aftertaste, truly makes you feel alive and in the mood for the festivities. "Refreshing. I wouldn't be surprised if Komari and her granddaughters went and blessed all the sake. It certainly is the sort of thing she'd do." Yeah... oh, you should refill her cup. "How considerate of you. Ah, the cherry blossoms are in full bloom, I cannot help but drink. So please, neither of us should hold back — it is a festival, after all." ] Like Kiyoko wanted, you've found an empty spot on one of the further branches, close to the wooden guardrails. The noise of the plaza, along with music, come to you distantly from ahead; behind you, clusters upon clusters of pink blossoms rich upon the boughs. Then, of course, there's the matter of the Frostwood, far, far beneath you... This high above the ground, it's easy for breezes to pick up, and every now and then a particularly strong gust sends loose pink petals floating through the air. Yeah, you may not be able to feel it like they do, but you can see why this sort of sight would inspire foxes to dedicate entire poems to extolling their beauty. "This is our spot. Not too far, neither too near — a special spot for the two of us, where our flower-viewing will not be disturbed, beloved." Kiyoko sighs and leans against you, resting her head on your shoulder.[pc.ra kitsune| Behind the two of you, one of her tails wraps its tip about yours, joined by another and another, until you're all warm and good inside and out.] "Will you try some of the food? I shall feed you, if that is your desire." Only if she lets you feed her, too. Reciprocity. "Ah, you make such a compelling argument, beloved; I find myself unable to protest. Very well, then." It's approaching noon now, and the hubbub from the courtyard-cum-plaza in confluence of the branches drifts over to you. It sure looks like it's getting lively, and numerous voices ring out in the by-now familiar lilting, refined words of the kitsune mother tongue. Even with Kiyoko sitting beside you and delicately popping seasoned seafood into your mouth and you doing the same for her, there is an aching inside of you; [pc.ra kitsune|even though you've literally sold your soul to look like these people, becoming one of them is going to require ever more effort on your part|once more, you're reminded of exactly how different you are from these foxy people, even though they've welcomed you with smiles and open arms]. Maybe when all this is done, you'll spend a little time properly learning how to be conversant in, if not literate in, this language without having to rely on others to translate for you... There's music, too, and as you look on, Miko and Mai take stage in the courtyard and start what looks like a ceremonial dance; they're dressed in full white Kerosite priestess' garments like Komari usually wears, and have fans in each of their hands as they twirl and gyrate their bodies amidst the falling pink petals. Their tails follow their movements, fluffy brushes painting pictures of quiet grace — no one would imagine that they're man-eating monsters on the side. "The girls are very good, aren't they?" They are indeed. "The sacred dances to the gods were the best part of the festivals," Kiyoko continues with a laugh. "I remember wanting to learn some when I was younger, and being told that while I could, it was something that would have to wait and come after my other duties. After all, even though I was descended from divinity and had the right to learn the dances, I had people like Komari to handle matters like that for me." Komari? Dance? "My retainer wasn't always short and dumpy, you know," Kiyoko says with a giggle, then points at Miko, still dancing away. "When she was younger, she looked a lot more like her great-great-granddaughter there. It happens to most of the women in her line when they get a bit older." Oh. "But enough about that, and more about me." Your fox-wife raises her chopsticks, prepared with another morsel. "Here, try some of this..." You move to bite down on Kiyoko's offering. Sushi rice made with thin fried tofu skin... ah, of course. Inarizushi, her favorite. She should have this herself instead of giving it to you... "There is more than enough, but you can feed me if you like. I see no cause for complaint[kiyoko.pregStage 1|, and the child within me is perpetually hungry]." She gives you a coy smile, and [kiyoko.pregStage 1|smooths her hands over her swollen belly|cosies in against you even more]. But of course. Such a spread — seafood, vegetable and fruit preserves alike, seaweed-wrapped rolls, even small pastries. If it came from Kohaku, it'd have — oh yes, of course the little golden fox would've included fish-shaped buns as well, taiyaki. "It's all meant to go well with the rice liquor, [kiyoko.pregStage 1 |but I can't have any as I am. That doesn't matter — the food is just as fine with amazake, and besides, anything tastes better when it's with you." There goes the flattery yet again. "It's in my nature as a fox. What am I to do?" |isn't it? Here, clean your palate with a drink between each so the flavors do not spoil each other." Even if the food is meant to be taken cold, it's truly delicious in a way that you wouldn't be able to find in the rest of the Marches. And to think you didn't notice anything behind the scenes when you last visited the den, given how much time and effort must have gone into it all..." "When you are fastidious and industrious as a matter of course, certainly being diligent is nothing out of place. But we should not be talking about work right now — it is a festival, after all. Here, have some more." Everything really tastes better when it's served by your faithful fox-wife... "That is my line, not yours." ] You cast out your gaze over the mass of ears, tails and fluff in the square once more. Miko and Mai's sacred dance is commanding most of the attention, but [kinu.isInari |off in the distance you spy Kinu and a pretty large fox-boy sitting off on one of the outer branches, a little more removed from the hustle and bustle like you are. The size difference between your daughter and her squeeze is pretty big, but then again if that's what she's into, who's to complain? It's clear what she sees in him, though — the poor boy listens thoughtfully, or at least appears to do so, while Kinu natters on animatedly. The one-sided conversation is occasionally punctuated by a squeeze or smack of her tail against him — it's actually quite cute how she can't quite reach her arms all the way around the poor kid... "Well, I suppose she's found someone who cares about her and she can care for, if nothing else," Kiyoko says glumly, her festive mood dampened by the sight. "While I don't really hold out much hope at this point, at least the boy is of good stock and breeding. That, and she's started noticing things other than dirt and plants." ... "But look at me complain like this. We're supposed to be enjoying ourselves today, are we not?" Indeed. |amongst the crowd you spy Kinu moving around between different parties, flitting about like the social butterfly she is. Always approachable yet carrying herself with the air and grace of a princess that sets her above those around her. A strange juxtaposition when you think about it, but that's easily smoothed over with a little charisma, isn't it? But whatever she's saying to each group she passes by, the other foxen seem absolutely enthralled by her words. Listening, eagerly, smiling, welcoming her with raised cups — Kinu herself practically embodies the spirit of the festivities, and while her pretty face does indeed help it can't be responsible for everything, can it? "They love her," Kiyoko says with a smile as she regards your daughter, too. "They love her, no matter what she says or does. She could tell the blandest joke, and they would laugh anyway, and genuinely so. They wouldn't remember what was so funny about it, but that she told it, and it was good. "It is for the best that I formally abdicated my position in favor of my sister's line as quickly as possible, and promised to remain in the colonies. If our daughter were allowed to return to her clan holdings or even worse, live in the capital and attend court... I might fear for her life. And if she did survive, and she probably would — her get might come to dominate the imperial court the way the Fujiwara did centuries ago before the shogunate came to be. That would not be healthy for anyone; there are twelve den mothers for a reason." You turn your gaze to Kinu once more; your daughter is toying with a gleeful fox kit, good-naturedly teasing the child with sweets while Nakano stands a respectful distance away as her escort for the proceedings. A princess, huh... well, there's something to be said for that. ] "But today is not just for others, but about us as well," your fox-wife continues, pouring you another cup of rice liquor. "So let us enjoy each others' company in our special spot, amidst the flowers Spring... is it not a splendid sight?" Mmm... sitting up in the branches, surrounded above, around and below by cherry blossoms, it's hard to deny that. Especially if your beloved fox-wife is right by your side. "There, look," Kiyoko purrs, [pc.ra kitsune |reaching around to gather one of your tails in her hands and fluff the fur up and down. Your breath catches in your throat as tingles shoot into the base of your tail and crawl up your spine, reaching all the way up to the tips of your ears before dissipating |reaching up over your shoulder and [pc.hasEmoteEars|teasing your ears|ruffling your [pc.hair]] ]. "Is all of this not a splendid view?" [var0] It is... "You have performed admirably as always, striving to accomplish many things," Kiyoko continues, [kiyoko.pregStage 1|pressing the warmth of her kit-filled belly against you|pouring another cup of liquor for herself and downing it in one gulp]. "[party.has kiyoko|And for some of these things, I too, have been by your side. ]But for today, since you chose to accompany me, allow yourself to be at ease, and come along." ... Come along with? Who? What? Kiyoko's fingers are warmer than you remember them usually being, and then you realize that with the faint sound of flint striking steel, ghostly blue sparks of foxfire spring up from where she caresses you. Her face is more than a little red, [kiyoko.pregStage 1|too|and the scent of liquor clings to her breath, as it must yours]... "Do not force yourself, beloved; it does not happen that way. Just simply look up at the blossoms, enjoy their shape and splendor, and slowly, slowly... allow yourself to be captivated by their beauty..." A stray petal falls on your nose. Kiyoko laughs, and flicks it away. She's openly pressing her body against you now, [kinu.isInari|in much the same way that Kinu was doing for her squeeze, ]and indeed, even through her yukata she's really flushed and heated...
rows.translation: 我觉得我们应该在那些较远的分支上找一个合适的地方。清子会告诉你的。不能离庆典现场太近，这样我们就能独处；但也不能太远，否则就看不到上面广场里发生的事情了。我想我找到了那个完美的位置。 结果就是，你按照你那位狐妖妻子的安排打开包裹，甚至用那块布作为你们两人的床铺。包裹里还有盒装食品、一张可折叠的木质小桌、更多的盒装食品、几瓶浓烈的米酒等等，甚至还有一个用狐火点燃的纸灯笼。显然，他们预计这些庆祝活动会持续到深夜。对于每一户家庭来说，这些活动至少要持续一个多小时——人们不禁会想知道，准备这一切需要花费多少时间，以及究竟有多少人参与了这些准备工作。你早就知道狐妖是非常挑剔的，但就连那些装在盒子里的食物，无论是配菜还是正餐，它们的摆放方式都是为了营造出美感与精致感——考虑到你对该活动的了解，这种设计确实恰到好处，但即便如此，还是让人觉得有些刻意。付出了这么多努力…… [kiyoko.pregStage 1 |在包里翻找其他物品时，清子找出了一个陶罐，轻轻闻了闻。清酒……这位千金小姐真是考虑周到，竟然想到了我最喜欢的东西。 你伸手去戳了戳你那位怀有身孕的狐狸妻子的肚子，惹得她咯咯笑了起来。这也难怪吧——她现在怀着孩子，当然不能喝酒了。 没关系。无论是盛开的樱花，还是美味的为了……的缘故亲爱的，没有人能与你相提并论。能与你一起外出，就已经是足够的理由了。 她可真会讨好别人，不是吗？唉，你也不能指望一只狐狸会没有巧舌如簧的本领吧…… |在那些瓶子中翻找着，清子抽出了其中一个，打开它闻了闻。对于那些偏远的乡村地区来说，我也想说——当地的酒类确实有着独特的风味。不一定更好，但确实更有趣味。阳光、土壤、雨水、稻米的品种，还有酿造工艺……过去，我母亲总会让人从全国各地把这些当地的酒类带到我们的家里。我真的很欣赏小毬选择使用当地的酒类而不是进口酒；我认为，这样会让这个场合显得更有意义。 嗯…… 清子给自己倒了一杯茶，放在那张矮矮的折叠桌上，然后把瓶子递给了你。来吧，亲爱的。你也喝一杯吧。 嗯，如果你想这么做的话，完全没问题。你可以用包装里提供的小杯子，让纪代子给你倒一些，然后像她那样一饮而尽。这种浓烈的米酒在你的胸腔和胃里燃烧起来，留下微微甜美的余味，真的会让你感到活着也正好处于享受这些庆祝活动的氛围中。 真是令人耳目一新。如果小毬和她的孙女们为这些清酒全都加持过，我一点也不会惊讶。这确实是她会做的事情。 嗯……哦，你该替她斟满酒杯。 你真是太体贴了。啊，樱花已经盛开了，我实在忍不住要喝一杯。所以，请大家都放开来吧——毕竟这是节日嘛。 ] 正如清子所希望的那样，你在一条较远的分支上找到了一个空位，那里靠近木制护栏。广场上的喧闹声以及音乐声从前方传来，而在你的身后，树枝上开满了成簇的粉色花朵。当然，还有那片位于你脚下深处的霜木林…… 而在这里，高高的空中，微风很容易将这些粉红色的花瓣卷起，偶尔，一阵特别强劲的风吹过，就会让这些花瓣飘荡在空气中。是啊，你可能无法像它们那样感受到那种情感，但你应该能理解，为什么这样的景象会激发狐妖们创作整首诗来赞美自己的美丽吧。 这是属于我们的地方。既不太远，也不太近——一个只属于我们两个人的特别地方，在这里观赏花朵时不会受到任何打扰，亲爱的。清子叹了口气，靠在你身上，将头放在你的肩膀上。[pc.ra kitsune| 在你们两人的身后，她的一条尾巴将它的尖端缠绕在你的尾巴上，接着又有另一条尾巴加入进来，一条又一条，直到你们所有人都感到温暖，从内到外都充满了温暖。] 你想尝尝这些食物吗？如果你愿意的话，我可以帮助你进食。 只有当她也允许你喂她的时候才行。这就是互惠原则。 啊，你提出的论点真是令人信服，亲爱的；我实在无法反驳。那好吧。 现在已经快到中午了，从那些被树枝环绕的庭院兼广场里传来的喧闹声逐渐传到了你的耳边。场面看起来确实越来越热闹了，许多声音用那种你已经熟悉了的、轻柔而优雅的狐族语言响彻在空气中。即使有清子坐在你身边，细心地将各种调味过的海鲜送入口中，而你也在为她做着同样的事，你的内心依然感到一阵隐隐的酸痛[pc.ra kitsune|尽管你为了变得像这些人一样，几乎不惜付出任何代价，但要想真正成为他们中的一员，你还需要付出更多的努力。|再一次，你清楚地意识到，自己与这些狡猾的人是多么的不同——尽管他们总是用微笑和热情的态度欢迎你。]也许等这一切都结束后，你可以花些时间认真学习这种语言，至少达到能够流利使用它的程度，这样就不再需要别人来为你翻译了…… 现场还有音乐相伴，这时米可和舞走上了庭院中的舞台，开始表演一种看起来像仪式舞蹈的动作。她们穿着与小毬通常所穿的相同的纯白色凯罗斯ite祭司服装，手中各拿一把扇子，随着粉色花瓣的飘落，她们旋转着身体，跳着这支舞蹈。它们的尾巴随着身体的动作而摆动，那些柔软的尾巴仿佛是一支支画笔，勾勒出一种宁静而优雅的画面——没有人会想到，这些生物实际上也是食人的怪物。 这些女孩都很优秀，不是吗？ 确实如此。 向神明献上的神圣舞蹈才是这些节庆活动中最精彩的部分。清子继续笑着说道。我记得小时候曾经想学习一些这样的东西，但当时有人告诉我可以这件事得等我完成其他任务之后再处理。毕竟，虽然我拥有神族的血统，也有权学习这些舞蹈，但像小毬这样的人，完全可以帮我处理这类事情。 蚊子？跳舞？ 你知道，我的保镖以前可并不总是矮胖的形象哦。清子笑着说道，然后指向仍在跳舞的米可。她年轻的时候，和那边那位曾曾孙女长得非常像。她这一辈的女性，大多数在年纪稍长之后都会出现这种情况。 哦。 不过，关于这个的话题就到此为止吧，让我们多聊聊我吧。你的狐妖妻子举起了筷子，准备再吃一小口。来，尝尝这些…… 你伸手去咬下清子的那份食物。用薄炸豆腐皮制成的寿司饭……啊，果然如此。这是她最喜欢的海苔寿司。她应该自己吃这份，而不是把它给你…… 足够多了，不过如果你想喂我，也完全可以。我觉得没有任何理由抱怨。[kiyoko.pregStage 1|而我内心的那个孩子，永远都处于饥饿的状态]。"她向你投来一个娇羞的微笑，然后[kiyoko.pregStage 1|她将双手轻轻放在自己隆起的腹部上。|它们会更加紧贴在你身上。]当然了。这样的美食种类繁多——有海鲜制品、蔬菜和水果蜜饯、用海藻包裹的面包卷，甚至还有各种小点心。如果这些食物是来自红霞岛的，那么——哦，对了，那只小金狐肯定也会加入鱼形面包吧。天妇罗。 这一切都是为了让它与米酒搭配得更加完美。 [kiyoko.pregStage 1 |但我现在的状况实在不适合享用那些食物。不过没关系，用米酒调味的话，食物依然会很好吃；而且，只要有你在身边，任何食物都会变得更加美味。 又来这套奉承话了。 作为一只狐狸，这就是我的天性。我该怎么办呢？ |不是吗？来，每尝一种食物后喝一杯饮料，这样各种味道就不会互相影响、破坏彼此的味道了。 即使这些食物本来是冷着吃的，但它们的美味程度确实是在其他地区无法找到的。想想看，上次你访问那个地方的时候，竟然没有注意到背后所花费的所有时间和精力…… 当你自然而然地变得一丝不苟、勤奋努力时，认真工作当然也是理所应当的。不过现在我们不应该谈论工作——毕竟这是节日嘛。来，再吃点吧。 当你那忠实的狐狸妻子为你端上这些美食时，一切似乎都变得更加美味了…… 那是我的台词，不是你的。 ] 你再次将目光投向广场上那些耳朵、尾巴和绒毛组成的景象。米可与麻衣的神圣舞蹈吸引了大多数人的注意，但[kinu.isInari |在远处，你看到了小娟和一个体型较大的狐狸男孩，他们坐在树枝的边缘，距离喧闹的人群要远一些，和你现在的位置差不多。你的女儿和她的伙伴之间的体型差距确实很大，但既然这是她喜欢的，谁又有资格去抱怨呢？不过，她对他究竟有什么感情，其实一目了然——那个可怜的小男孩认真地听着她说话，至少表面上是这样；而小娟则兴致勃勃地不停唠叨。这种单方面的对话，偶尔会被她用尾巴轻触他一下或拍打他一下来打断……其实，她那双手臂根本伸不到那个可怜的小男孩身边，这种样子还挺可爱的…… 嗯，我想她终于找到了一个关心她、也能照顾她的人吧。清子沮丧地说道，这一幕让她的节日气氛彻底破灭了。虽然我现在其实并不抱太大希望，但至少这个男孩出身良好，家世也不错。而且，她也开始注意一些除了泥土和植物之外的东西了。 …… 但是看看我，正在这样抱怨。今天我们应该是来享受乐趣的，不是吗？ 确实如此。 |在人群中，你看到小娟穿梭于不同的团体之间，就像一只善于交际的蝴蝶一样自由自在地活动。她总是平易近人，但同时又带着公主般的高贵与优雅，这使得她与周围的人截然不同。仔细想想，这种对比确实有些奇怪，但只要稍微发挥一点魅力，这些问题就能轻易得到解决，不是吗？ 然而，无论她对遇到的每一群狐狸说了些什么，其他的狐狸们似乎都被她的话语彻底吸引住了。大家聚精会神地听着，脸上洋溢着笑容，举杯欢迎她的到来——小娟本人简直就是这场庆祝活动的象征。当然，她那漂亮的面容确实为这一切增色不少，但这一切的成就，却不能仅仅归功于她的容貌。一切可以吗？ 他们爱她。清子微笑着，同时也看着你的女儿说道。无论她说什么、做什么，他们都爱她。哪怕她讲的笑话再平淡无奇，他们也会发笑，而且是发自内心的笑。他们可能记不清那个笑话到底有什么好笑的地方，但他们记得是她讲的，而且那个笑话确实很好笑。 为了大家的利益着想，我尽快正式放弃了我的职位，让我的妹妹继承我的位置，并且承诺会留在殖民地。如果我们的女儿能够回到她的家族领地，或者更糟的是，能够住在首都并参加宫廷活动的话，那才是最好的结果。我可能会为她担心她的安危。而如果她真的活了下来——她很可能会活下来——她的势力可能会像几个世纪前藤原家族在幕府建立之前那样，主导整个朝廷。这对任何人来说都不是好事；之所以会有十二位“堂母”，也是有着原因的。" 你再次将目光转向小娟；你的女儿正在和一个活泼可爱的小狐狸玩耍，一边开心地用糖果逗弄那个孩子，而中野则站在稍远的地方，作为她的护卫，陪伴着她完成这些活动。一位公主啊……嗯，这也确实有它的意义。 ] 但今天不仅仅是为了别人，也与我们自己息息相关。你的狐妖妻子继续说着，又给你倒了一杯米酒。那么，让我们在这个充满鲜花的地方，一起享受彼此的陪伴吧。春天……这景象难道不美妙吗？ 嗯……坐在树枝上，周围上下全是樱花，这种感觉确实很难忽视。尤其是当你亲爱的狐妖妻子就在你身边时。 看，就是那里。清子发出呼噜声， [pc.ra kitsune |她伸手抓住你的尾巴，轻轻地将毛茸茸的尾巴毛捋来捋去。你的呼吸顿时变得急促起来，因为一阵阵刺痛感从尾巴根部开始，一路沿着脊椎向上蔓延，最终传到了耳尖，然后才逐渐消失 rows.raw: ' "I think we should find a nice spot on one of the further branches," Kiyoko tells you. "Not too close to the festivities so that we can be by ourselves, and yet not too far so that we can still see what's going on in the upper plaza. I think I know just the place." So it happens that you unpack your bundle at your fox-wife's discretion, using the cloth itself as a ground sheet for the two of you. Boxed food, a small collapsable wooden low table, plenty of boxed food, several bottles of strong rice liquor and the like — there's even a paper lantern made to be lit with foxfire. Clearly, they expect the festivities to stretch into the night. At least one of these each for over a hundred families — you can only wonder how long it took to prepare all this, and the number of hands that were involved. You knew foxes were fastidious, but the way even the food in the boxes from side dishes to whole meals is arranged is intended to evoke beauty and mindfulness — not inappropriate given what you understand of the event, but still. So much effort... [kiyoko.pregStage 1 |Digging through the other stuff in the package, Kiyoko fishes out a clay jar and gives it a dainty sniff. "Amazake. How thoughtful for the golden girl to provide my favorite." You reach out and poke your fox-wife's kit-filled belly, eliciting a giggle from her. It's not surprising; she can't have liquor when she's with child. "That's fine. Whether it's cherry blossoms in full bloom or delicious sake, none are a match for you, beloved. Going out with you would have been reason enough." She really knows how to flatter, doesn't she? Ah well, you can't expect a fox to have anything but a silver tongue... |Digging through the bottles, Kiyoko pulls out one of them and pops it open to give it a sniff. "I will say this for rural backwaters, too — the local flavors of liquor are always something. Not necessarily better, but more interesting; the sun, the soil, the rain, the breed of rice, the brewing process — back in the day, my mother would have them brought from all over the Old Country to our holdings. I do appreciate Komari using the local brew instead of importing; it gives the occasion a lot more meaning, I believe." Hmm... Kiyoko pours herself a cup, setting it out on the low folding table, then holds out the bottle to you. "Come, beloved. Have a cup as well." Well, don't mind if you do. You take up one of the small cups provided in the package and let Kiyoko pour you some, then down it as she does hers. The fire the strong rice liquor lights in your chest and stomach, with its slightly sweet aftertaste, truly makes you feel alive and in the mood for the festivities. "Refreshing. I wouldn't be surprised if Komari and her granddaughters went and blessed all the sake. It certainly is the sort of thing she'd do." Yeah... oh, you should refill her cup. "How considerate of you. Ah, the cherry blossoms are in full bloom, I cannot help but drink. So please, neither of us should hold back — it is a festival, after all." ] Like Kiyoko wanted, you've found an empty spot on one of the further branches, close to the wooden guardrails. The noise of the plaza, along with music, come to you distantly from ahead; behind you, clusters upon clusters of pink blossoms rich upon the boughs. Then, of course, there's the matter of the Frostwood, far, far beneath you... This high above the ground, it's easy for breezes to pick up, and every now and then a particularly strong gust sends loose pink petals floating through the air. Yeah, you may not be able to feel it like they do, but you can see why this sort of sight would inspire foxes to dedicate entire poems to extolling their beauty. "This is our spot. Not too far, neither too near — a special spot for the two of us, where our flower-viewing will not be disturbed, beloved." Kiyoko sighs and leans against you, resting her head on your shoulder.[pc.ra kitsune| Behind the two of you, one of her tails wraps its tip about yours, joined by another and another, until you're all warm and good inside and out.] "Will you try some of the food? I shall feed you, if that is your desire." Only if she lets you feed her, too. Reciprocity. "Ah, you make such a compelling argument, beloved; I find myself unable to protest. Very well, then." It's approaching noon now, and the hubbub from the courtyard-cum-plaza in confluence of the branches drifts over to you. It sure looks like it's getting lively, and numerous voices ring out in the by-now familiar lilting, refined words of the kitsune mother tongue. Even with Kiyoko sitting beside you and delicately popping seasoned seafood into your mouth and you doing the same for her, there is an aching inside of you; [pc.ra kitsune|even though you've literally sold your soul to look like these people, becoming one of them is going to require ever more effort on your part|once more, you're reminded of exactly how different you are from these foxy people, even though they've welcomed you with smiles and open arms]. Maybe when all this is done, you'll spend a little time properly learning how to be conversant in, if not literate in, this language without having to rely on others to translate for you... There's music, too, and as you look on, Miko and Mai take stage in the courtyard and start what looks like a ceremonial dance; they're dressed in full white Kerosite priestess' garments like Komari usually wears, and have fans in each of their hands as they twirl and gyrate their bodies amidst the falling pink petals. Their tails follow their movements, fluffy brushes painting pictures of quiet grace — no one would imagine that they're man-eating monsters on the side. "The girls are very good, aren't they?" They are indeed. "The sacred dances to the gods were the best part of the festivals," Kiyoko continues with a laugh. "I remember wanting to learn some when I was younger, and being told that while I could, it was something that would have to wait and come after my other duties. After all, even though I was descended from divinity and had the right to learn the dances, I had people like Komari to handle matters like that for me." Komari? Dance? "My retainer wasn't always short and dumpy, you know," Kiyoko says with a giggle, then points at Miko, still dancing away. "When she was younger, she looked a lot more like her great-great-granddaughter there. It happens to most of the women in her line when they get a bit older." Oh. "But enough about that, and more about me." Your fox-wife raises her chopsticks, prepared with another morsel. "Here, try some of this..." You move to bite down on Kiyoko's offering. Sushi rice made with thin fried tofu skin... ah, of course. Inarizushi, her favorite. She should have this herself instead of giving it to you... "There is more than enough, but you can feed me if you like. I see no cause for complaint[kiyoko.pregStage 1|, and the child within me is perpetually hungry]." She gives you a coy smile, and [kiyoko.pregStage 1|smooths her hands over her swollen belly|cosies in against you even more]. But of course. Such a spread — seafood, vegetable and fruit preserves alike, seaweed-wrapped rolls, even small pastries. If it came from Kohaku, it'd have — oh yes, of course the little golden fox would've included fish-shaped buns as well, taiyaki. "It's all meant to go well with the rice liquor, [kiyoko.pregStage 1 |but I can't have any as I am. That doesn't matter — the food is just as fine with amazake, and besides, anything tastes better when it's with you." There goes the flattery yet again. "It's in my nature as a fox. What am I to do?" |isn't it? Here, clean your palate with a drink between each so the flavors do not spoil each other." Even if the food is meant to be taken cold, it's truly delicious in a way that you wouldn't be able to find in the rest of the Marches. And to think you didn't notice anything behind the scenes when you last visited the den, given how much time and effort must have gone into it all..." "When you are fastidious and industrious as a matter of course, certainly being diligent is nothing out of place. But we should not be talking about work right now — it is a festival, after all. Here, have some more." Everything really tastes better when it's served by your faithful fox-wife... "That is my line, not yours." ] You cast out your gaze over the mass of ears, tails and fluff in the square once more. Miko and Mai's sacred dance is commanding most of the attention, but [kinu.isInari |off in the distance you spy Kinu and a pretty large fox-boy sitting off on one of the outer branches, a little more removed from the hustle and bustle like you are. The size difference between your daughter and her squeeze is pretty big, but then again if that's what she's into, who's to complain? It's clear what she sees in him, though — the poor boy listens thoughtfully, or at least appears to do so, while Kinu natters on animatedly. The one-sided conversation is occasionally punctuated by a squeeze or smack of her tail against him — it's actually quite cute how she can't quite reach her arms all the way around the poor kid... "Well, I suppose she's found someone who cares about her and she can care for, if nothing else," Kiyoko says glumly, her festive mood dampened by the sight. "While I don't really hold out much hope at this point, at least the boy is of good stock and breeding. That, and she's started noticing things other than dirt and plants." ... "But look at me complain like this. We're supposed to be enjoying ourselves today, are we not?" Indeed. |amongst the crowd you spy Kinu moving around between different parties, flitting about like the social butterfly she is. Always approachable yet carrying herself with the air and grace of a princess that sets her above those around her. A strange juxtaposition when you think about it, but that's easily smoothed over with a little charisma, isn't it? But whatever she's saying to each group she passes by, the other foxen seem absolutely enthralled by her words. Listening, eagerly, smiling, welcoming her with raised cups — Kinu herself practically embodies the spirit of the festivities, and while her pretty face does indeed help it can't be responsible for everything, can it? "They love her," Kiyoko says with a smile as she regards your daughter, too. "They love her, no matter what she says or does. "It is for the best that I formally abdicated my position in favor of my sister's line as quickly as possible, and promised to remain in the colonies. If our daughter were allowed to return to her clan holdings or even worse, live in the capital and attend court... I might fear for her life. And if she did survive, and she probably would — her get might come to dominate the imperial court the way the Fujiwara did centuries ago before the shogunate came to be. That would not be healthy for anyone; there are twelve den mothers for a reason." You turn your gaze to Kinu once more; your daughter is toying with a gleeful fox kit, good-naturedly teasing the child with sweets while Nakano stands a respectful distance away as her escort for the proceedings. A princess, huh... well, there's something to be said for that. ] "But today is not just for others, but about us as well," your fox-wife continues, pouring you another cup of rice liquor. "So let us enjoy each others' company in our special spot, amidst the flowers Spring... is it not a splendid sight?" Mmm... sitting up in the branches, surrounded above, around and below by cherry blossoms, it's hard to deny that. Especially if your beloved fox-wife is right by your side. "There, look," Kiyoko purrs, [pc.ra kitsune |reaching around to gather one of your tails in her hands and fluff the fur up and down. Your breath catches in your throat as tingles shoot into the base of your tail and crawl up your spine, reaching all the way up to the tips of your ears before dissipating |reaching up over your shoulder and [pc.hasEmoteEars|teasing your ears|ruffling your [pc.hair]] ]. rows.original: You think over the offer a moment, and eventually shake your head sadly. You'd like to go, but the fact of the matter is that you're tired and you'd probably end up embarrassing your fox-family in this state. Maybe next year? Kiyoko nods, her face carefully blank and neutral as she accepts your decision. "Well, beloved, if you would watch the house for us while we're gone, that would be very much appreciated." You can do as much. For now, a bit of rest, perhaps? "Of course. Come and sleep, my love." When dawn breaks the next day, the space next to you on the futon is distinctly devoid of Kiyoko. Nor, for that matter is Kinu to be found in [kinu.isInari|the fields|her chambers] [kiyoko.numKits 1 2 3 |and her sister is similarly missing |and the other kits are similarly missing ]; they must have left before dawn.[kiyoko.numKits 8| The den is usually so alive with the sound of activity and voices all around, and to hear the silence brought about by the lack of fox children is a little disquieting.] Nevertheless, you take the day off in the fox den, generally lazing around and recovering your strength from the ardors of your adventures. The tranquility of Kiyoko's home makes for a refreshing recuperation, and nothing arrives to spoil your day; Kiyoko was kind enough to leave boxed meals in the kitchen for you before she left, so you don't even have to nip down to Hawkethorne to grab a bite to eat. By the time you're done with your soak in the hot spring by the edge of the crater, you're feeling light in body, clear in mind, and could definitely take on the entire world at once. Eventually, though, Kiyoko and Kinu return in the evening, a little ruffled about the edges but still holding their prim and proper demeanour. You catch them walking down the path from the torii gate, and sweep your fox-wife into a welcoming hug, which she greedily reciprocates. How was it? Did she have fun? "Like I said, I do enjoy those little backwater festivals. They may not be very grand, but I find them filled with a lot more genuine spirit than any I experienced as a girl in the capital when my mother brought me there. I always preferred the ones at my clan holdings..." Aha. And how about Kinu? Your daughter just blushes; that tells you all you need to know. Well then, it looks like that's that, then. Time for you to be the one to invite your fox-wife to bed this time around...
rows.translation: 你仔细考虑了一下这个提议，最终还是遗憾地摇了摇头。你确实很想去，但现实是，你太累了，以现在的状态去的话，只会让你的狐狸家族感到难堪。也许明年吧？ 清子点了点头，她的表情刻意保持中立，默默接受了你的决定。嗯，亲爱的，如果在我们不在的时候你能帮忙照看一下房子，那我们将不胜感激。 你可以做你想做的任何事。不过现在，或许应该稍微休息一下吧？ 当然可以。来吧，亲爱的，一起睡觉吧。 第二天黎明到来时，你躺在榻榻米上时身边的位置显然已经空无一人——纪代子已经不在那里了。而纪野，也同样不见了。 [kinu.isInari|这些领域|她的房间] [kiyoko.numKits 1 2 3 |她的妹妹也同样失踪了。 |其他套件也同样缺失。 ]他们肯定是在黎明之前离开的。[kiyoko.numKits 8| 通常，这个巢穴里总是充满了各种活动声和人们的谈话声，而如今因为没有狐狸幼崽而陷入的寂静，确实让人感到有些不安。] 尽管如此，你还是会在狐狸窝里休息一天，通常会懒洋洋地躺着，恢复在冒险中消耗的体力。清子家的宁静环境为你的恢复提供了理想的条件，没有任何事情会打扰你的一天；清子在离开之前还特意在厨房里留下了盒装餐食，因此你甚至不必特意去鹰棘镇找东西吃。当你在火山口边缘的温泉中泡完澡后，会感到身体轻松、头脑清醒，简直有勇气去面对整个世界了。 不过，到了晚上，清子和小雪还是回来了，虽然有些疲惫，但依然保持着她们那端庄得体的举止。你看到他们正沿着那条小路走下来。鸟居你推开门，将你的狐狸妻子拥入怀中，而她也贪婪地回抱了你。 感觉怎么样？她玩得开心吗？ 正如我所说，我确实很喜欢那些偏远地区的节日。虽然它们可能并不十分盛大，但我觉得其中蕴含的真诚与热情，远超过我小时候母亲带我去首都参加的那些节日。我一直更喜欢我们家族举办的那些节日…… 啊哈，那小娟呢？ 你的女儿只是脸红了，这就说明了一切。那么，看来事情就是这样了。是时候你这次要由我来邀请你的“狐狸妻子”上床……

I think the ancient Belharans had a similar ceremony known as kissing the ring — a public acknowledgement of authority and display of fealty from vassal to lord, from subject to ruler. Of course, the cultural contexts are hardly the same, but the idea is consistent; the public servants of the colonies shall affirm their undying loyalty to me as their liege, and I shall of course, graciously affirm my responsibilities towards them in return." All by patting them on the head. "One by one, yes." As far as you understand Kiyoko's situation, though, won't the fact that she's consolidating her power base here in the colonies cause concern across the ocean, especially given that she abdicated for just that? To not raise concern? "It is not a matter you should be worried about," Kiyoko replies. "In centuries past, the capital largely ignored the outer provinces save for what could be milked out of them; today, it is the colonies that suffer that same fate. So long as I do not directly threaten their petty intrigue, they do not care what goes on across the ocean — to their detriment, of course. "I may not have any formal power in that sense any more, but I still have my title and its privileges, and as such obligations are made of me. Laws without people are but simple words on paper, that is all. Either way, it is a simple acknowledgement of what is, and that is in and of itself important — the reification and formalization of such relationships such that everyone knows they exist, and for duties and obligations to be placed upon them." You think you understand, but at the same time you get the feeling that with as with everything to do with these foxes, there's a lot of subtext which you should know, what with being [pc.ra kitsune |physically one |Kiyoko's consort ] and all, but that's a worry that you realistically can't do anything about. So, she wants you to come along, is that right? "It is not mandatory that you attend, but I would certainly appreciate it if you did, beloved," Kiyoko replies. "That, and the ceremony is almost certain to run from dawn to dusk, so [party.has kiyoko |you will have to wait until the day after before we can resume our travels |I will by necessity not be around to entertain you, should you linger at home ]. Either way, the day will be occupied... so you might as well attend, is that not right?" '

Fine. In that case, do you actually need to dress up or something? It sounds like the occasion where you would... |鉴于你们俩的关系如此亲密，她邀请你作为她的配偶一同前往，这完全合情合理。没有什么比亲眼看到你可爱的狐狸妻子以正式的身份履行职责更令你开心的了，而且你相信她一定能够做得非常出色。毕竟，她具备这样的气质和风度 ]。[pc.ra kitsune | 当然，还有你作为凯罗斯的冠军这一身份——在这种情况下，你实际上就已经有义务这么做必须参加。如果你没有参加的话……嗯，那你肯定违反了狐族那些复杂而繁琐的礼仪规则。 |]当然，在此之前你可能从未听说过这种“轻拍头部的仪式”，但既然这是为了庆贺清子，你也应该愿意尝试一下吧。[pc.bgMulti noblescion slumrat | 你本身出身贵族，所以你很清楚这些事情的重要性——虽然你在社会等级中地位不够高，没有资格在这些仪式中发言，但仍然必须参加。这与你过去参加过的其他仪式相比，又有何不同呢？ | 确实，考虑到你出生时的那些不幸境遇，在这样的环境中你会感到格格不入，但你不能永远保持这种状态。从那以后，你在生活中取得了很大的进步，完全依靠自己的努力取得了成功，现在是时候去适应新的环境了。正如那句俗话所说：你可以把老鼠从贫民窟里带走，但却无法消除贫民窟本身；我对这句话的信任，丝毫不亚于你年轻时听过的那些半真半假的民间传说。 ] |嗯，好的。妈妈，[kinu.Dad]你们为什么不去一起享受彼此的陪伴呢？我得去处理那些红薯了。 |纪久耸了耸肩，故作夸张地打了个哈欠，还扭动着肩膀，用喉咙里发出懒洋洋的狐妖叫声来表示自己很困。“好吧，行吧。妈妈[kinu.Dad]晚安，我真的累坏了——好孩子应该跟着太阳一起睡觉呢。” “好孩子应该会换上合适的睡衣再睡觉，而不是穿着工作服就直接躺下。” “在正常情况下，是的，但在这种环境下，穿着符合场合要求的正式服装其实是一种奢侈。你穿平时的衣服也没关系……至少在这种情况下没有问题。[kinu.isInari | 话虽如此，我还是希望我们的女儿在参加这样的活动时，不要穿工作服…… ] 无论如何，一切都已经为我们准备好了——场所的清洁、所需的材料、适当的装饰等等。我们所要做的，就是完成最重要的环节——也就是举行仪式本身。”基约科轻声说道，同时将她那柔软的尾巴轻轻抚在你的背上。“完全没有压力，我们现在就可以出发了吧？
